bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 春，正月，東羌先零圍祋祤，掠雲陽，當煎諸種復反。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Eastern Qiang Xianlian besieged Fufeng, plundered Yunyang, and the various Dangjian tribes rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, the Eastern Qiang Xianlian band besieged Fufeng, raided Yunyang, and the Dangjian tribes rose in revolt once more.

sentences.zh: 段熲擊之於鸞鳥，大破之，西羌遂定。

translations.literal: Duan Yong attacked them at Luanniao, inflicted a great defeat on them, and the Western Qiang were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong routed them at Luanniao in a crushing victory, and the Western Qiang were finally brought to order.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王夫台寇玄菟；

translations.literal: The king of Fuyu, Futai, raided Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Futai, king of Fuyu, invaded Xuantu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 玄菟太守公孫域擊破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator of Xuantu, Gongsun Yu, defeated and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yu, the grand administrator of Xuantu, drove him off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，先零羌寇三輔，攻沒兩營，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Xianlian Qiang raided the Three Metropolises, captured and destroyed two camps, and killed more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, the Xianlian Qiang struck the Three Metropolises, overran two garrisons, and killed more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬子晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the last day of the month, renzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renzi day, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 陳蕃既免，朝臣震慄，莫敢復為黨人言者。

translations.literal: After Chen Fan had been dismissed, the court officials were shaken with fear, and none dared again to speak on behalf of the partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen Fan was removed from office, the court was terrified, and no one dared speak up for the partisans again.

sentences.zh: 賈彪曰：「吾不西行，大禍不解。

translations.literal: Jia Biao said, "If I do not go west, the great calamity will not be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Biao said, "Unless I go west myself, this great disaster will never be undone.

sentences.zh: 」乃入雒陽，說城門校尉竇武、尚書魏郡霍諝等，使訟之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon entered Luoyang, persuaded the Commandant of the City Gates Dou Wu, the Master of Writing Huo Xu of Wei Commandery, and others, and had them plead the case.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went to Luoyang, won over Commandant of the City Gates Dou Wu, Master of Writing Huo Xu of Wei Commandery, and others, and urged them to press the case at court.

sentences.zh: 武上疏曰：「陛下即位以來，未聞善政，常侍、黃門，競行譎詐，妄爵非人。

translations.literal: Dou Wu submitted a memorial saying, "Since Your Majesty's accession, no good governance has been heard of; the Regular Attendants and the Yellow Gates compete in deceit and treachery, recklessly enfeoffing unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu submitted a memorial: "Since Your Majesty came to the throne, we have heard of no worthy policies; the eunuch attendants vie with one another in deceit and bestow titles on unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 伏尋西京，佞臣執政，終喪天下。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the Western Capital, when flatterers held power, they ultimately lost All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Western Capital: when sycophants held sway, the dynasty lost the realm in the end.

sentences.zh: 今不慮前事之失，復循覆車之軌。

translations.literal: Now, without considering the errors of past affairs, you again follow the track of an overturned cart.
translations.idiomatic: Today you take no lesson from past failures and again follow the path of the overturned cart.

sentences.zh: 臣恐二世之難，必將復及，趙高之變，不朝則夕。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the disaster of the Second Emperor will soon come again, and a transformation like Zhao Gao's—not morning but evening.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the catastrophe of the Second Emperor will return, and a coup like Zhao Gao's may come not in months but in days.

sentences.zh: 近者奸臣牢修造設黨議，遂收前司隸校尉李膺等逮考，連及數百人。

translations.literal: Recently the wicked minister Wang Fu fabricated partisan accusations, then arrested the former Director of the Retainers Li Ying and others for examination, implicating several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the villain Wang Fu invented the partisan purge, had the former Director of the Retainers Li Ying and others seized for interrogation, and dragged several hundred men into the net.

sentences.zh: 曠年拘錄，事無效驗。

translations.literal: For years they have been held in custody, yet the cases have no corroborating evidence.
translations.idiomatic: They have languished in prison for years, yet no proof has ever been found.

sentences.zh: 臣惟膺等建忠抗節，志經王室，此誠陛下稷、伊、呂之佐；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Ying and the others established loyalty and resisted perversity, their will set on sustaining the royal house—these are truly Your Majesty's aides like Ji, Yi, and Lü.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, Ying and his fellows have shown loyal resolve and stood firm against corruption, their hearts set on the royal house—they are truly ministers of the caliber of Hou Ji, Yi Yin, and Lü Wang.

sentences.zh: 而虛為奸臣賊子之所誣枉，天下寒心，海內失望。

translations.literal: Yet they have been falsely slandered by wicked ministers and villainous sons; all under Heaven chill at heart, and within the seas men lose hope.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wicked officials and their accomplices have framed them on false charges; the empire is disheartened and the realm has lost faith.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下留神澄省，時見理出，以厭人鬼喁喁之心。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty attend with clear judgment, timely release those with sound reason, and thereby satisfy the clamoring hearts of men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty examine the matter with clear judgment, release the innocent in good time, and so quiet the uproar of both the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 今台閣近臣，尚書朱寓、荀緄、劉祐、魏朗、劉矩、尹勳等，皆國之貞士，朝之良佐；

translations.literal: Now the nearby ministers of the Secretariat—Masters of Writing Zhu Yu, Xun Yun, Liu You, Wei Lang, Liu Ju, Yin Xun, and others—are all upright men of the state and excellent assistants of the court.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers close at hand in the Secretariat—Zhu Yu, Xun Yun, Liu You, Wei Lang, Liu Ju, Yin Xun, and the rest—are all men of integrity and fine servants of the throne.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎張陵、媯皓、苑康、楊喬、邊韶、戴恢等，文質彬彬，明達國典，內外之職，群才並列。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing Attendants Zhang Ling, Gui Hao, Yuan Kang, Yang Qiao, Bian Shao, Dai Hui, and others are refined in both culture and substance, clear in state institutions; for posts within and without, talents stand side by side.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant masters of writing—Zhang Ling, Gui Hao, Yuan Kang, Yang Qiao, Bian Shao, Dai Hui, and others—combine learning and integrity and understand the laws of the realm; for every office, within the court and beyond, able men stand ready.

sentences.zh: 而陛下委任近習，專樹饕餮，外典州郡，內干心膂，宜以次貶黜，案罪糾罰；

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty entrusts power to close favorites, exclusively raising gluttonous parasites who govern provinces and commanderies without and meddle with the heart and sinews within—they should be demoted in due order, their crimes investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty relies on cronies and nurtures greedy parasites who rule the provinces abroad and meddle with the core of government at home—they should be demoted in turn, their crimes investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 信任忠良，平決臧否，使邪正毀譽，各得其所，寶愛天官，唯善是授，如此，咎徵可消，天應可待。

translations.literal: Trust the loyal and good, judge right and wrong fairly, let the praise and blame of the crooked and straight each find its place, cherish the offices of Heaven and grant them only to the worthy—thus omens of blame may be dispelled and Heaven's response awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Trust loyal men, judge merit and fault fairly, let the worthy and the wicked each receive their due, honor the offices of state and give them only to the capable—then ill omens will fade and Heaven's favor may be won.

sentences.zh: 間者有嘉禾、芝草、黃龍之見。

translations.literal: Recently there have appeared auspicious grain, spirit fungus, and yellow dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Of late there have been reports of fine grain, spirit fungus, and yellow dragons.

sentences.zh: 夫瑞生必於嘉士，福至實由善人，在德為瑞，無德為災。

translations.literal: Auspicious signs arise only where there are excellent men; blessings in truth come through good men—in virtue they are omens of fortune, without virtue they are calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Omens appear only where worthy men dwell; blessings truly come through good men—with virtue they are auspicious, without virtue they are disasters.

sentences.zh: 陛下所行不合天意，不宜稱慶。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's conduct does not accord with Heaven's intent; it is not fitting to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's conduct does not accord with Heaven's will; you ought not to celebrate.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，因以病上還城門校尉、槐裡侯印綬。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, he thereupon pleaded illness and returned the seals and ribbon of Commandant of the City Gates and Marquis of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was in, he pleaded illness and returned the seals and ribbon of his posts as Commandant of the City Gates and Marquis of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 霍諝亦為表請。

translations.literal: Huo Xu also submitted a memorial pleading on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Xu likewise submitted a memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 帝意稍解，因中常侍王甫就獄訊黨人范滂等，皆三木囊頭，暴於階下，甫以次辨詰曰：「卿等更相拔舉，迭為脣齒，其意如何？

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was somewhat eased, and he had the Regular Attendant Wang Fu go to the prison to question the partisans Fan Pang and others, all with the three cangues and heads bagged, exposed below the steps; Wang Fu questioned them in turn, saying, "You gentlemen repeatedly promote and recommend one another, taking turns as lip and teeth—what is your intent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented somewhat and sent Regular Attendant Wang Fu to the prison to question the partisans Fan Pang and others, who wore the triple cangue with their heads hooded and were displayed on the steps below. Wang Fu questioned them one by one: "You keep promoting and recommending one another, acting as each other's mouthpiece—what is your purpose?

sentences.zh: 」滂曰：「仲尼之言：『見善如不及，見惡如探湯。

translations.literal: " Fan Pang said, "Confucius said: 'Seeing good as if one cannot reach it, seeing evil as if touching boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Pang replied, "Confucius said: 'When you see what is good, hurry toward it as if you cannot catch up; when you see what is evil, shrink from it as if from scalding water.

sentences.zh: 』滂欲使善善同其清，惡惡同其污，謂王政之所願聞，不悟更以為黨。

translations.literal: ' Pang wished to make the good share in purity and the evil share in defilement—this, he thought, was what royal governance would wish to hear; he did not realize it would instead be taken as factionalism.
translations.idiomatic: ' I wanted the good to share in purity and the wicked to share in shame—I thought that was what good government should hear. I never imagined it would be called forming a faction.

sentences.zh: 古之修善，自求多福。

translations.literal: In antiquity, cultivating goodness was seeking much blessing for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: In old times, doing good brought blessings on oneself.

sentences.zh: 今之修善，身陷大戮。

translations.literal: Today, cultivating goodness means the body falls into great execution.
translations.idiomatic: Today, doing good means falling under the executioner's blade.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，願埋滂於首陽山側，上不負皇天，下不愧夷、齊。

translations.literal: On the day of my death, I wish to be buried on the slope of Mount Shouyang—I will not fail Heaven above, nor shame Yi and Qi below.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, bury me on the slopes of Mount Shouyang—then I shall not fail Heaven above nor shame Yi and Qi below.

sentences.zh: 」甫愍然為之改容，乃得並解桎梏。

translations.literal: " Wang Fu was moved with compassion and changed his expression; they were all able to have their shackles removed together.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Fu was moved and his manner changed; they were all released from their shackles.

sentences.zh: 李膺等又多引宦官子弟，宦官懼，請帝以天時宜赦。

translations.literal: Li Ying and the others had also implicated many sons of eunuch officials; the eunuchs were afraid and asked the emperor that the season was suitable for an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying and the others had also implicated many sons of eunuch families; the eunuchs grew afraid and urged the emperor that the season called for a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚申，赦天下，改元；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengshen, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengshen day, the empire was granted a general amnesty and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 黨人二百餘人皆歸田裡，書名三府，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: More than two hundred partisans all returned to their villages; their names were recorded in the Three Excellencies' offices and they were barred from office for life.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred partisans were sent home; their names were entered in the registers of the Three Excellencies and they were barred from office for life.

sentences.zh: 范滂往候霍諝而不謝。

translations.literal: Fan Pang went to visit Huo Xu but did not thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Pang called on Huo Xu but did not thank him.

sentences.zh: 或讓之，滂曰：「昔叔向不見祁奚，吾何謝焉！

translations.literal: Someone reproached him for this; Pang said, "In former times Shu Xiang did not visit Qi Xi—why should I offer thanks!
translations.idiomatic: When someone reproached him, Pang said, "In antiquity Shu Xiang did not go to see Qi Xi—why should I offer thanks?

sentences.zh: 」滂南歸汝南，南陽士大夫迎之者，車數千兩，鄉人殷陶、黃穆侍衛於旁，應對賓客。

translations.literal: " Pang returned south to Runan; the gentry and officials of Nanyang who came to welcome him numbered several thousand carriages, while his fellow villagers Yin Tao and Huang Mu attended at his side, receiving and answering guests.
translations.idiomatic: " Pang went south to Runan. Gentry and officials from Nanyang turned out to welcome him in thousands of carriages; his fellow villagers Yin Tao and Huang Mu attended him and received guests on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 滂謂陶等曰：「今子相隨，是重吾禍也！

translations.literal: Pang said to Tao and the others, "Your following me now only deepens my calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Pang told Tao and the others, "Your accompanying me now only makes my disaster worse!

sentences.zh: 」遂遁還鄉里。

translations.literal: " He thereupon slipped away and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: " He slipped away and went home in secret.

sentences.zh: 初，詔書下舉鉤黨，郡國所奏相連及者，多至百數，唯平原相史弼獨無所上。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the edict went out to investigate and implicate partisans, what the commanderies and kingdoms reported as mutually implicated often reached into the hundreds; only the Chancellor of Pingyuan, Shi Bi, submitted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict went out to hunt down partisans, most commanderies and kingdoms reported chains of names running into the hundreds; only Shi Bi, the chancellor of Pingyuan, submitted no names at all.

sentences.zh: 詔書前後迫切州郡，髡笞掾史，從事坐傳捨責曰：「詔書疾惡黨人，旨意懇惻。

translations.literal: Edicts came repeatedly, pressing the provinces and commanderies; clerks were shaved and flogged. The Investigator, sitting in the relay station, reproached him, saying, "The edict hates and detests the partisans; its intent is earnest and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Edict after edict pressed the provinces; clerks were beaten and cropped. The investigator, lodged at the relay station, rebuked him: "The edict condemns the partisans in the strongest terms; its intent is urgent and sincere.

sentences.zh: 青州六郡，其五有黨，平原何治而得獨無？

translations.literal: Of Qingzhou's six commanderies, five have partisans—by what governance does Pingyuan alone have none?
translations.idiomatic: Five of Qingzhou's six commanderies have reported partisans—what sort of rule leaves Pingyuan alone without any?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「先王疆理天下，畫界分境，水土異齊，風俗不同。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "The former kings demarcated All Under Heaven, drew boundaries and divided territories—water and soil differ, customs are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi replied, "The former kings divided the realm, drew boundaries and set borders—lands differ in soil and water, and customs are not the same.

sentences.zh: 它郡自有，平原自無，胡可相比！

translations.literal: Other commanderies have them by nature; Pingyuan naturally has none—how can they be compared!
translations.idiomatic: Other commanderies have them; Pingyuan simply does not—how can you compare the two?

sentences.zh: 若承望上司，誣陷良善，淫刑濫罰，以逞非理，則平原之人，戶可為黨。

translations.literal: If, to curry favor with superiors, one falsely implicates the good, applies excessive punishments and reckless penalties to gratify injustice, then every household in Pingyuan could be made partisans.
translations.idiomatic: If I curried favor with my superiors, framed the innocent, and abused the law to satisfy injustice, then every household in Pingyuan could be called a partisan.

sentences.zh: 相有死而已，所不能也！

translations.literal: A chancellor has only death—that is what he cannot do!
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor I would rather die than do such a thing!

sentences.zh: 」從事大怒，即收郡僚職送獄，遂舉奏弼。

translations.literal: " The Investigator was greatly angered, immediately arrested the commandery officials and sent them to prison, and then memorialized against Bi.
translations.idiomatic: " The investigator flew into a rage, had the commandery staff arrested and thrown into prison, and memorialized against Bi.

sentences.zh: 會黨禁中解，弼以俸贖罪。

translations.literal: It happened that the partisan prohibition was lifted midway; Bi redeemed his offense with his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The partisan prohibition was lifted before long, and Bi paid a fine from his salary to clear the charge.

sentences.zh: 所脫者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those he had spared were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The number he had spared was very great.

sentences.zh: 竇武所薦：朱寓，沛人；

translations.literal: Those recommended by Dou Wu: Zhu Yu, a man of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Those Dou Wu had recommended included Zhu Yu of Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 苑康，勃海人；

translations.literal: Yuan Kang, a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kang of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 楊喬，會稽人；

translations.literal: Yang Qiao, a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiao of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 邊韶，陳留人。

translations.literal: Bian Shao, a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Shao of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 喬容儀偉麗，數上言政事，帝愛其才貌，欲妻以公主，喬固辭，不聽，遂閉口不食，七日而死。

translations.literal: Qiao's bearing and appearance were grand and handsome; he repeatedly submitted opinions on state affairs. The emperor loved his talent and looks and wished to give him a princess in marriage. Qiao firmly declined; when the emperor would not listen, he closed his mouth and ate nothing, and after seven days died.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was tall and striking in appearance and often submitted opinions on government affairs. The emperor admired his talent and looks and wished to marry him to a princess. Qiao refused firmly; when the emperor would not relent, he stopped eating and died after seven days.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，巴部言黃龍見。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Ba Commandery reported that a yellow dragon had appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, Ba Commandery reported that a yellow dragon had been seen.

sentences.zh: 初，郡人欲就池浴，見池水濁，因戲相恐，「此中有黃龍，」語遂行民間，太守欲以為美。

translations.literal: Earlier, people of the commandery wished to bathe in a pool; seeing the pool water muddy, they joked in frightening one another, "There is a yellow dragon in here," and the words spread among the people. The Grand Administrator wished to take this as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, locals had gone to bathe in a pool; seeing the water was murky, they joked in fright that "there is a yellow dragon in here," and the story spread. The grand administrator wanted to treat it as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 故上之。

translations.literal: Therefore he reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: So he reported it to the court.

sentences.zh: 郡吏傅堅諫曰：「此走卒戲語耳。

translations.literal: The commandery official Fu Jian remonstrated, saying, "This is merely the jesting talk of runners and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery clerk Fu Jian remonstrated: "That is only soldiers' idle talk.

sentences.zh: 」太守不聽。

translations.literal: " The Grand Administrator would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The grand administrator would not listen.

sentences.zh: 六月大水，勃海海溢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month there was great flooding; the Bohai Sea overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month came great floods, and the Bohai Sea overflowed its shores.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，先零羌寇三輔，張奐遣司馬尹端、董卓拒擊，大破之，斬其酋豪，首虜萬餘人，三州清定。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Xianlian Qiang raided the Three Metropolises. Zhang Huan sent his Major Yin Duan and Dong Zhuo to resist and attack; they inflicted a great defeat, beheaded their chieftains and nobles, and took more than ten thousand heads and captives; the three provinces were pacified and settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, the Xianlian Qiang raided the Three Metropolises. Zhang Huan sent his major Yin Duan and Dong Zhuo to meet them, won a crushing victory, slew their chieftains, and took more than ten thousand heads and captives; the three border provinces were pacified.

sentences.zh: 奐論功當封，以不事宦官故不果封，唯賜錢二十萬，除家一人為郎。

translations.literal: Huan's merit was judged worthy of enfeoffment, but because he did not cultivate the eunuchs he was not in fact enfeoffed; he was only granted two hundred thousand cash and one man of his household was made a Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: By rights Zhang Huan deserved a fief for his merit, but because he would not court the eunuchs he received no title—only two hundred thousand cash and an appointment as gentleman for one member of his household.

sentences.zh: 奐辭不受，請徙屬弘農。

translations.literal: Huan declined and would not accept, requesting instead to transfer his household registration to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan refused the reward and asked to move his household registration to Hongnong instead.

sentences.zh: 舊制，邊人不得內徙，詔以奐有功，特許之。

translations.literal: By old regulation, frontier people could not move inward; an edict, because Huan had merit, specially permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, frontier households were not allowed to move inland; an edict made an exception for Zhang Huan because of his service.

sentences.zh: 拜董卓為郎中。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo was appointed Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was appointed a gentleman at the palace.

sentences.zh: 卓，隴西人，性粗猛有謀，羌胡畏之。

translations.literal: Zhuo was a man of Longxi; by nature coarse, fierce, and resourceful—the Qiang and Hu feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was a native of Longxi, rough and fierce by nature but shrewd, and the Qiang and the Hu feared him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，復癭陶王悝為勃海王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renshen, the Marquis of Yingtao, Liu Ti, was restored as King of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen day, Liu Ti was restored from Marquis of Yingtao to King of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，帝崩於德陽前殿。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the emperor died in the front hall of Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, the emperor died in the front hall of Deyang.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，尊皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day, the empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后臨朝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager presided over the court.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager assumed regency over the court.

sentences.zh: 初，竇後既立，御見甚稀，唯采女田聖等有寵。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Empress Dou had been established, the emperor's visits to her were very rare; only the palace women Tian Sheng and others had favor.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dou was installed, the emperor rarely visited her chamber; only palace ladies such as Tian Sheng enjoyed his favor.

sentences.zh: 後素忌忍，帝梓宮尚在前殿，遂殺田聖。

translations.literal: The empress had always been jealous and harsh; the emperor's coffin was still in the front hall, yet she thereupon killed Tian Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had always been jealous and cruel; even while the emperor's coffin still lay in the front hall, she had Tian Sheng put to death.

sentences.zh: 城門校尉竇武議立嗣，召侍御史河間劉鰷，問以國中宗室之賢者，鯈稱解瀆亭侯宏。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the City Gates Dou Wu deliberated on establishing an heir; he summoned the Attendant Imperial Clerk Liu Tao of Hejian and asked which members of the imperial clan within the state were worthy. Tao named the Marquis of Jiedu, Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the City Gates Dou Wu deliberated on the succession and summoned Attendant Imperial Clerk Liu Tao of Hejian, asking which members of the imperial house were worthy. Tao named Marquis Hong of Jiedu.

sentences.zh: 宏者，河間孝王之曾孫也，祖淑，父萇，世封解瀆亭侯。

translations.literal: Hong was the great-grandson of King Xiao of Hejian; his grandfather was Shu, his father Chang—the family had been enfeoffed for generations as Marquises of Jiedu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was the great-grandson of King Xiao of Hejian; his grandfather was Shu and his father Chang—the family had held the marquisate of Jiedu for generations.

sentences.zh: 武乃入白太后，定策禁中，以鯈守光祿大夫，與中常侍曹節並持節將中黃門、虎賁、羽林千人，奉迎宏，時年十二。

translations.literal: Wu thereupon entered to inform the empress dowager; the decision was fixed within the palace. Tao was made Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; together with the Regular Attendant Cao Jie, each holding credentials, they led a thousand Central Yellow Gates, Tiger Guards, and Feathered Forest guards to welcome Hong—he was then twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu went in to inform the empress dowager, and the choice was settled within the palace. Tao was made acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he and Regular Attendant Cao Jie, each bearing credentials, led a thousand guards from the Central Yellow Gate, Tiger Guards, and Feathered Forest to escort Hong to the capital—he was twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 孝靈皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Ling, First Part, Upper Section.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling, Part One, Section One.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬午，以城門校尉竇武為大將軍。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renwu, the Commandant of the City Gates Dou Wu was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on renwu day, Commandant of the City Gates Dou Wu was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 前太尉陳蕃為太傅，與武及司徒胡廣參錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The former Grand Commandant Chen Fan was made Grand Tutor; together with Wu and the Minister over the Masses Hu Guang, he participated in recording matters for the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Former Grand Commandant Chen Fan was made Grand Tutor and, with Dou Wu and Minister over the Masses Hu Guang, shared oversight of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時新遭大喪，國嗣未立，諸尚書畏懼，多托病不朝。

translations.literal: At this time they had newly suffered the great mourning; the heir to the state was not yet established; the various Masters of Writing were afraid, and many pleaded illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just entered deep mourning and the heir was not yet enthroned; many masters of writing were afraid and stayed away from court on pretext of illness.

sentences.zh: 陳蕃移書責之曰：「古人立節，事亡如存。

translations.literal: Chen Fan sent a letter reproaching them, saying, "The ancients established integrity—serving the departed as if they were present.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan sent a letter rebuking them: "The ancients upheld integrity by serving the dead as if they still lived.

sentences.zh: 今帝祚未立，政事日蹙，諸君奈何委荼蓼之苦，息偃在床，於義安乎！

translations.literal: Now the imperial succession is not yet established and state affairs grow daily more pressing—how can you gentlemen cast off the bitter hardship of tucao and tumu, resting supine upon your beds—is this right in principle!
translations.idiomatic: Today the throne stands empty and government grows more urgent by the day—how can you abandon your duties to the bitter hardship of the realm and lie abed—is that righteous conduct?

sentences.zh: 」諸尚書惶怖，皆起視事。

translations.literal: " The various Masters of Writing were fearful and alarmed; all rose to attend to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: " The masters of writing were terrified and all returned to their posts.

sentences.zh: 己亥，解瀆亭侯至夏門亭，使竇武持節，以王青蓋車迎入殿中；

translations.literal: On jihai, the Marquis of Jiedu arrived at Xiamen Pavilion; Dou Wu was sent bearing credentials to welcome him into the palace with the prince's green-canopied carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day, Marquis Hong of Jiedu reached Xiamen Pavilion; Dou Wu was sent with credentials to welcome him into the palace in the prince's green-canopied carriage.

sentences.zh: 庚子，即皇帝位，改元。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he took the imperial throne and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day he ascended the throne and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛酉，葬孝桓皇帝於宣陵，廟曰威宗。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinyou, Emperor Xiaohuan was buried at Xuan Mausoleum; his temple name was Weizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou day, Emperor Xiaohuan was buried at Xuan Mausoleum with the temple name Weizong.

sentences.zh: 辛未，赦天下。

translations.literal: On xinwei, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初，護羌校尉段熲既定西羌，而東羌先零等種猶未服，度遼將軍皇甫規、中郎將張奐招之連年，既降又叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Protector of the Qiang Duan Yong had pacified the Western Qiang, the Eastern Qiang Xianlian and other tribes were still not submissive. The General Who Crosses the Liao Huangfu Gui and the General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhang Huan had summoned them for years—they would submit and then rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Protector of the Qiang Duan Yong had pacified the Western Qiang, the Eastern Qiang Xianlian and other tribes remained unsubdued. General Who Crosses the Liao Huangfu Gui and General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhang Huan had spent years trying to win them over, but they submitted only to rebel again.

sentences.zh: 桓帝詔問熲曰：「先零東羌造惡反逆，而皇甫規、張奐各擁強眾，不時輯定，欲令熲移兵東討，未識其宜，可參思術略。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan issued an edict asking Yong, "The Xianlian Eastern Qiang have committed evil and rebelled, yet Huangfu Gui and Zhang Huan each command strong hosts and have not timely pacified them. We wish to have Yong shift troops east to attack—we do not yet know whether this is fitting; you may reflect and consider strategy and plans.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan asked Yong by edict: "The Xianlian Eastern Qiang have risen in wicked rebellion, yet Huangfu Gui and Zhang Huan each command large forces and have not pacified them in good time. We wish to send you east with your troops—we are not sure whether that is wise; consider the strategy and advise us.

sentences.zh: 」熲上言曰：「臣伏見先零東羌雖數叛逆，而降於皇甫規者，已二萬許落；

translations.literal: " Yong submitted a statement saying, "Your servant has observed that although the Xianlian Eastern Qiang have repeatedly rebelled, those who have submitted to Huangfu Gui already number about twenty thousand encampments.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong replied: "I observe that although the Xianlian Eastern Qiang have rebelled repeatedly, some twenty thousand encampments have already submitted to Huangfu Gui.

sentences.zh: 善惡既分，餘寇無幾。

translations.literal: Good and evil are already divided; the remaining bandits are few.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and the hostile are already separated; only a few rebels remain.

sentences.zh: 今張奐躊躇久不進者，當慮外離內合，兵往必驚。

translations.literal: Now the reason Zhang Huan hesitates and has long not advanced is surely that he fears those outside will separate while those within unite—if troops go, they will certainly be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan's long hesitation to advance surely stems from fear that those outside will unite with those within—if troops march in, the tribes will panic and rally together.

sentences.zh: 且自冬踐春，屯結不散，人畜疲羸，有自亡之勢，欲更招降，坐制強敵耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, from winter through spring they have camped and gathered without dispersing; men and livestock are weary and emaciated, with a tendency to destroy themselves—he wishes again to summon surrender and thereby control a strong enemy while sitting still.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from winter into spring they have camped together without dispersing; men and livestock are exhausted and weak and are on the verge of collapse on their own. He means to win them over again and thereby control a formidable foe without fighting.

sentences.zh: 臣以為狼子野心，難以恩納，勢窮雖服，兵去復動；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that a wolf cub has the heart of a wolf—hard to win with kindness; though they submit when cornered, when the troops depart they stir again.
translations.idiomatic: In my view they have the nature of wolf cubs and cannot be won by kindness; though they submit when desperate, they rebel again once the army withdraws.

sentences.zh: 唯當長矛挾脅，白刃加頸耳！

translations.literal: Only with long spears at their ribs and bare blades at their necks!
translations.idiomatic: Only long spears at their ribs and naked blades at their throats will do!

sentences.zh: 計東種所餘三萬餘落，近居塞內，路無險所，非有燕、齊、秦、趙從橫之勢，而久亂並、涼，累侵三輔，西河、上郡，已各內徙，安定、北地，復至單危。

translations.literal: It is calculated that the Eastern tribes remaining number more than thirty thousand encampments; they dwell near the inner side of the passes, with no perilous terrain on the roads—they do not have the crisscross strength of Yan, Qi, Qin, and Zhao—yet they have long troubled Bing and Liang, repeatedly raiding the Three Metropolises; Xihe and Shang Commandery have each moved inward, and Anding and Beidi are again reduced to utter peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern tribes still number more than thirty thousand encampments. They live close inside the frontier passes where the roads offer no natural barriers; they do not enjoy the strategic depth of Yan, Qi, Qin, and Zhao. Yet they have long ravaged Bing and Liang, repeatedly struck the Three Metropolises, and forced the relocation of Xihe and Shang—Anding and Beidi are again in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 自雲中、五原，西至漢陽二千餘里，匈奴、諸羌，並擅其地，是為癰疽伏疾，留滯脅下，如不加誅，轉就滋大。

translations.literal: From Yunzhong and Wuyuan west to Hanyang, more than two thousand li—the Xiongnu and the various Qiang together monopolize that land. This is an abscess and a hidden malady lodged beneath the ribs; if they are not punished, it will turn and grow ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From Yunzhong and Wuyuan west to Hanyang stretches more than two thousand li of territory now held by the Xiongnu and the Qiang tribes. This is an abscess festering at the empire's side; if we do not destroy them, the wound will only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 若以騎五千、步萬人、車三千兩，三冬二夏，足以破定，無慮用費為錢五十四億，如此，則可令群羌破盡，匈奴長服，內徙郡縣，得反本土。

translations.literal: If with five thousand cavalry, ten thousand infantry, and three thousand chariots, in three winters and two summers it would be sufficient to break and settle them—estimated expense about five hundred forty million cash—thus one could cause the Qiang tribes to be utterly broken, the Xiongnu to submit for long, and the inwardly relocated commanderies and counties to return to their native lands.
translations.idiomatic: With five thousand cavalry, ten thousand foot soldiers, and three thousand chariots, three winters and two summers would suffice to crush and pacify them at an estimated cost of five hundred forty million cash. Then the Qiang could be broken completely, the Xiongnu brought to lasting submission, and the relocated frontier commanderies restored to their homelands.

sentences.zh: 伏計永初中，諸羌反叛，十有四年，用二百四十億；

translations.literal: Your servant calculates: from the Yongchu era, when the various Qiang rebelled—for fourteen years, two thousand four hundred million were spent;
translations.idiomatic: I reckon that from the Yongchu era, when the Qiang tribes rose in rebellion, the empire spent two thousand four hundred million cash over fourteen years;

sentences.zh: 永和之末，復經七年，用八十餘億。

translations.literal: at the end of Yonghe, again seven years passed, using more than eight hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: and from the end of the Yonghe era through another seven years, more than eight hundred million cash besides.

sentences.zh: 費耗若此，猶不誅盡，餘孽復起，於茲作害。

translations.literal: Expenditure like this, yet still not exterminated to the last; remnant evils rise again and at this time cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: After such expense, the enemy was still not destroyed; remnant bands rose again and continue to ravage the realm.

sentences.zh: 今不暫疲民，則永寧無期。

translations.literal: If now one does not temporarily weary the people, then lasting peace has no appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: If we will not burden the people for a season now, lasting peace will never come.

sentences.zh: 臣庶竭駑劣，伏待節度。

translations.literal: Your servant will exhaust my feeble capacity and humbly await command and control.
translations.idiomatic: I will give all my poor strength and await your orders.

sentences.zh: 」帝許之，悉聽如所上，熲於是將兵萬餘人，繼十五日糧，從彭陽直指高平，與先零諸種戰於逢義山。

translations.literal: " The Emperor assented and entirely approved as submitted; Yong thereupon led troops of more than ten thousand, carrying fifteen days' provisions, from Pengyang straight toward Gaoping, and fought the Xianlian and various tribes at Fengyi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the plan in full. Yong then led more than ten thousand men with fifteen days' rations, marched from Pengyang straight on Gaoping, and fought the Xianlian tribes at Fengyi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 虜兵盛，熲眾皆恐。

translations.literal: The barbarian troops were strong; all of Yong's host were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy force was overwhelming, and Yong's men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 熲乃令軍中長鏃利刃，長矛三重，挾以強弩，列輕騎為左右翼，謂將士曰：「今去家數千里，進則事成，走必盡死，努力共功名！

translations.literal: Yong then ordered the army: long arrowheads and sharp blades, triple ranks of long spears, flanked with powerful crossbows; he arrayed light cavalry as left and right wings, and told the officers and soldiers, "Now we are thousands of li from home—advance and the affair succeeds; flee and all will die—strive together for fame and merit!
translations.idiomatic: Yong ordered long arrowheads and keen blades, three ranks of long spears backed by strong crossbows, and light cavalry on both wings. He told his officers and men: "We are thousands of li from home. Advance, and we prevail; retreat, and we perish. Fight for glory together!"

sentences.zh: 」因大呼，眾皆應聲騰赴，馳騎於傍，突而擊之，虜眾大潰，斬首八千餘級。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he shouted loudly; all responded and leapt forward; cavalry galloped on the flanks and charged into the attack; the barbarian host was utterly routed, with more than eight thousand heads cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He gave a great shout. The whole army surged forward at once; horsemen swept in from the flanks and struck. The enemy broke completely, and more than eight thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 太后賜詔書褒美曰：「須東羌盡定，當並錄功勤；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager bestowed an edict praising him, saying, "Wait until the Eastern Qiang are entirely pacified, and merit and diligence will be recorded together;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sent an edict of praise: "When the Eastern Qiang are fully pacified, your full merit will be recorded;

sentences.zh: 今且賜熲錢二十萬，以家一人為郎中。

translations.literal: for now bestow on Yong two hundred thousand cash and appoint one member of his household as a Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: for now grant Yong two hundred thousand cash and appoint one member of his household as a Gentleman of the Palace."

sentences.zh: 」敕中藏府調金錢、彩物增助軍費，拜熲破羌將軍。

translations.literal: " She ordered the palace treasury to allocate gold cash and colored goods to augment military expenses, and appointed Yong General Who Breaks the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: She also ordered the palace treasury to supply gold, cash, and goods for the army, and appointed Yong General Who Breaks the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 閏月，甲午，追尊皇祖為孝元皇，夫人夏氏為孝元後，考為孝仁皇，尊帝母董氏為慎園貴人。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiawu, the imperial grandfather was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaoyuan, Lady Xia as Empress Xiaoyuan, the father as Emperor Xiaoren, and the Emperor's mother Lady Dong was honored as Honored Lady of Shenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jiawu day, the imperial grandfather was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaoyuan, Lady Xia as Empress Xiaoyuan, the father as Emperor Xiaoren, and the Emperor's mother Lady Dong was made Honored Lady of Shenyuan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰，太尉周景薨，司空宣酆免；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on wuchen, Grand Commandant Zhou Jing died; Minister of Works Xuan Feng was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuchen day, Grand Commandant Zhou Jing died and Minister of Works Xuan Feng was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 以長樂衛尉王暢為司空。

translations.literal: Wang Chang, Palace Guard of Changle, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang, Palace Guard of Changle, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day of dingwei, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of dingwei, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 以太中大夫劉矩為太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Palace Secretary Liu Ju was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Palace Secretary Liu Ju was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 六月，京師大水。

translations.literal: Sixth month, the capital region suffered great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the capital was struck by severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，錄定策功，封竇武為聞喜侯，武子機為渭陽侯，兄子紹為鄠侯，靖為西鄉侯，中常侍曹節為長安鄉侯，侯者凡十一人。

translations.literal: On guisi, accomplishments in settling the succession were recorded; Dou Wu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenxi, Wu's son Ji as Marquis of Weiyang, his brother's son Shao as Marquis of Hu, Jing as Marquis of Xixiang, and Regular Palace Attendant Cao Jie as Marquis of Chang'an District—in all eleven were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day, those who had settled the succession were rewarded: Dou Wu was made Marquis of Wenxi; his son Ji, Marquis of Weiyang; his brother's sons Shao and Jing, Marquises of Hu and Xixiang; Regular Palace Attendant Cao Jie, Marquis of Chang'an District—eleven ennoblements in all.

sentences.zh: 涿郡盧植上書說武曰：「足下之於漢朝，猶旦、奭之在周室，建立聖主，四海有系，論者以為吾子之功，於斯為重。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi of Zhuo Commandery submitted a letter advising Wu, saying, "Your relation to the Han dynasty is like that of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao to the Zhou house—you established a sage ruler and the realm has its bond; commentators hold that your achievement, my lord, is weightiest at this juncture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi of Zhuo Commandery wrote to Dou Wu: "Your place in the Han house is like that of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao in the Zhou dynasty—you raised a worthy sovereign and secured the realm. Men of judgment hold that among all your deeds, this is the greatest."

sentences.zh: 今同宗相後，披圖案牒，以次建之，何勳之有！

translations.literal: Now successors from the same clan succeed each other in turn—unroll the charts and registers and establish them in order—what merit is there in that!
translations.idiomatic: Yet succession within one clan follows charts and registers in fixed order. What merit lies in that?

sentences.zh: 豈可橫叨天功，以為己力乎！

translations.literal: How can one presumptuously claim Heaven's merit as one's own strength!
translations.idiomatic: How can you seize Heaven's credit and call it your own achievement!

sentences.zh: 宜辭大賞，以全身名。

translations.literal: You ought to decline the great rewards to preserve body and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Decline these great honors to preserve your life and name.

sentences.zh: 」武不能用。

translations.literal: " Wu could not adopt this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wu would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 植身長八尺二寸，音聲如鐘，性剛毅，有大節。

translations.literal: Zhi was eight chi and two inches in height, his voice like a bell; by nature bold and resolute, with great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi stood eight chi and two inches tall, spoke in a voice like a bell, and was by nature stern and resolute, a man of great principle.

sentences.zh: 少事馬融，融性豪侈，多列女倡歌舞於前，植侍講積年，未嘗轉眄，融以是敬之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Ma Rong; Rong's nature was lavish and extravagant, and he often arrayed female entertainers singing and dancing before him; Zhi served at lectures for many years and never once turned his eyes aside—Rong therefore respected him for this.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Ma Rong, who lived lavishly and kept singing girls and dancers before him. Zhi attended his lectures for years without once glancing aside, and Rong came to respect him for it.

sentences.zh: 太后以陳蕃舊德，特封高陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, because of Chen Fan's longstanding virtue, specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gaoyang District.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Chen Fan's long service and virtue, the Empress Dowager specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gaoyang District.

sentences.zh: 蕃上疏讓曰：「臣聞割地之封，功德是為。

translations.literal: Fan submitted a memorial declining, saying, "Your servant has heard that grants of territory and enfeoffment are for merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Fan submitted a memorial of refusal: "I have heard that fiefs and titles are granted for merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣雖無素潔之行，竊慕君子『不以其道得之，不居也』。

translations.literal: Though your servant lacks a record of unstained conduct, I privately admire the maxim of the noble man: 'What is not obtained by the proper Way, one does not occupy.'
translations.idiomatic: I cannot claim unstained conduct, yet I honor the saying of the noble man: what is not gained by the proper Way, one does not accept."

sentences.zh: 若受爵不讓，掩面就之，使皇天振怒，災流下民，於臣之身，亦何所寄！

translations.literal: If I accept the title without declining and cover my face to take it, causing August Heaven to stir in anger and calamities to flow down upon the people—what would your servant's person have to rely upon!
translations.idiomatic: If I take this title without refusing, I would invite Heaven's wrath and bring disaster on the people. What honor would remain to me?

sentences.zh: 」太后不許。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 蕃固讓，章前後十上，竟不受封。

translations.literal: Fan firmly declined; memorials before and after were submitted ten times, and in the end he did not accept the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Fan persisted in refusing and submitted ten memorials in all, and in the end never accepted the title.

sentences.zh: 段熲將輕兵追羌，出橋門，晨夜兼行，與戰於奢延澤、落川、令鮮水上，連破之；

translations.literal: Duan Yong led light troops in pursuit of the Qiang, exiting Qiao Gate, traveling day and night without pause; he fought at Sheyan Marsh, Luochuan, and Lingxian River and repeatedly broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong pursued the Qiang with light forces through Qiao Gate, marching day and night. He fought them at Sheyan Marsh, Luochuan, and Lingxian River and defeated them again and again;

sentences.zh: 又戰於靈武谷，羌遂大敗。

translations.literal: he fought again at Lingwu Valley, and the Qiang were then utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: then fought them again at Lingwu Valley, and the Qiang suffered a great rout.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，熲至涇陽，餘寇四千落，悉散入漢陽山谷間。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Yong reached Jingyang; the remaining bandits, four thousand encampments, all scattered into the mountain valleys of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yong reached Jingyang. Four thousand remaining encampments scattered into the mountain valleys of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 護匈奴中郎將張奐上言：「東羌雖破，餘種難盡，段熲性輕果，慮負敗難常，宜且以恩降，可無後悔。

translations.literal: Protector of the Xiongnu, General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhang Huan submitted a statement, saying, "Although the Eastern Qiang are broken, the remnant tribes are hard to exterminate; Duan Yong's nature is rash and impulsive—I fear defeat is hard to guard against—it would be fitting for now to win them with kindness, so there will be no regrets.
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Xiongnu Zhang Huan submitted a memorial: "The Eastern Qiang are broken, but the remnant tribes cannot easily be wiped out. Duan Yong is rash and reckless; defeat may come when least expected. Better to win them with kindness now and avoid regret later."

sentences.zh: 」詔書下熲，熲復上言：「臣本知東羌雖眾，而軟弱易制，所以比陳愚慮，思為永寧之算，而中郎將張奐說虜強難破，宜用招降。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued to Yong; Yong again submitted a statement, saying, "Your servant originally knew that although the Eastern Qiang were numerous, they were weak and easy to control—therefore I earlier set forth my foolish considerations, thinking to devise a plan for lasting peace; yet General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhang Huan argued the barbarians were strong and hard to break and that summoning surrender should be used.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was sent to Yong, who replied: "I knew all along that though the Eastern Qiang were numerous, they were weak and manageable. That is why I urged a plan for lasting peace. Zhang Huan argued that the tribes were too strong to crush and that we should win them by surrender."

sentences.zh: 聖朝明監，信納瞽言，故臣謀得行，奐計不用。

translations.literal: The sage court clearly observed and trusted my blind counsel, so my plan was carried out and Huan's plan was not used.
translations.idiomatic: The court saw clearly and accepted my counsel, so my plan went forward and Huan's did not.

sentences.zh: 事勢相反，遂懷猜恨，信叛羌之訴，飾潤辭意，雲臣兵『累見折衄，又言『羌一氣所生，不可誅盡，山谷廣大，不可空靜，血流污野，傷和致災。

translations.literal: The situation ran contrary; he therefore harbored suspicion and resentment, believed the complaints of the rebel Qiang, adorned and embellished his words, saying my troops 'have repeatedly suffered defeats,' and again saying 'the Qiang are born of one breath—they cannot be exterminated to the last; the valleys and mountains are vast—they cannot be emptied and stilled; blood flows and stains the wilds, harming harmony and bringing calamity.'
translations.idiomatic: When matters turned against him, he grew suspicious and resentful. He believed the rebel Qiang's complaints and dressed them up in fine words, claiming my army 'has suffered defeat after defeat,' and saying 'the Qiang share one breath and cannot be exterminated; the mountains and valleys are vast and cannot be emptied; blood will soak the fields, disturb harmony, and bring disaster.'"

sentences.zh: 』臣伏念周、秦之際，戎狄為害，中興以來，羌寇最盛，誅之不盡，雖降復叛。

translations.literal: " Your servant humbly reflects: at the time of Zhou and Qin, the Rong and Di were harmful; since the restoration, Qiang raids have been most severe—exterminate them without finishing, and though they submit they rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect: from Zhou and Qin onward the Rong and Di have been a scourge, but since the restoration no raiders have been worse than the Qiang. Destroy them incompletely, and they submit only to rebel again.

sentences.zh: 今先零雜種，累以反覆，攻沒縣邑，剽略人物，發塚露屍，禍及生死，上天震怒，假手行誅。

translations.literal: Now the Xianlian mixed tribes have repeatedly turned back and forth—they have attacked and overrun counties and towns, plundered people and goods, opened graves and exposed corpses; calamity reaches the living and the dead; August Heaven is stirred to anger and uses another's hand to carry out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianlian and their allies have turned again and again: they have overrun counties and towns, plundered the people, opened graves and exposed the dead. Their evil touches both the living and the dead. Heaven is enraged and has lent us its hand to punish them.

sentences.zh: 昔邢為無道，衛國伐之，師興而雨；

translations.literal: Formerly when Xing acted without the Way, the state of Wei attacked them, and when the army marched, rain fell;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Xing ruled wickedly, Wei marched against them and rain fell as the army set out;

sentences.zh: 臣動兵涉夏，連獲甘澍，歲時豐稔，人無疵疫。

translations.literal: your servant moved troops through summer and repeatedly received sweet timely rain; the year's harvest was abundant and the people suffered no pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: I have campaigned through summer and received timely rain again and again. The harvest has been rich and the people free of plague.

sentences.zh: 上佔天心，不為災傷；

translations.literal: Above, I observe Heaven's heart—it is not harmed by calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven shows no sign of wrath;

sentences.zh: 下察人事，眾和師克。

translations.literal: below, I examine human affairs—the host is harmonious and the army prevails.
translations.idiomatic: on earth the troops are united and victories come.

sentences.zh: 自橋門以西、落川以東，故宮縣邑，更相通屬，非為深險絕域之地，車騎安行，無應折衄。

translations.literal: From Qiao Gate west and Luochuan east, the former commanderies, counties, and towns connect with one another in succession—it is not deep peril and utterly remote territory; chariots and horsemen travel safely; there is no reason troops should suffer defeat.
translations.idiomatic: From Qiao Gate west to Luochuan east, old commanderies and counties lie in linked succession. This is no trackless wilderness; chariots and horsemen can pass safely. There is no cause for repeated defeat.

sentences.zh: 案奐為漢吏，身當武職，駐軍二年，不能平寇，虛欲修文戢戈，招降獷敵，誕辭空說，僭而無征。

translations.literal: Consider that Huan is an officer of Han, personally holding a military post; he stationed troops for two years and could not pacify the bandits; he vainly wished to cultivate culture and sheathe weapons, win over fierce enemies by surrender—empty talk and wild words, lofty claims without proof.
translations.idiomatic: Huan is an officer of Han in command of troops. He camped two years and could not pacify the enemy, yet talks of culture and peace, of winning fierce foes by surrender—empty words, grand claims without deed.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How do I say this?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 昔先零作寇，趙充國徙令居內，煎當亂邊，馬援遷之三輔，始服終叛，至今為鯁，故遠識之士，以為深憂。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Xianlian raided, Zhao Chongguo moved them inside at Lingju; the Jiandang troubled the borders; Ma Yuan relocated them to the Three Metropolises—they submitted at first but rebelled in the end, and to this day remain a bone stuck in the throat; therefore men of farseeing wisdom have taken this as deep cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianlian first raided, Zhao Chongguo moved them within at Lingju; the Jiandang troubled the frontier; Ma Yuan resettled them in the Three Metropolises. They submitted at first and rebelled in the end, and remain a bone in the throat to this day. Men of foresight have long feared exactly this.

sentences.zh: 今傍郡戶口單少，數為羌所創毒，而欲令降徒與之雜居，是猶種枳棘於良田，養虺蛇於室內也。

translations.literal: Now the neighboring commanderies have households that are few and sparse, repeatedly harmed by the Qiang, yet you wish to have surrendered captives live mixed among them — this is like planting bitter orange thorns in fertile fields, or raising poisonous serpents within one's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The border commanderies are thinly populated and have suffered repeated ravages at the hands of the Qiang. To settle surrendered tribes among them would be like sowing thorn trees in good farmland, or keeping vipers in one's own house.

sentences.zh: 故臣奉大漢之威，建長久之策，欲絕其本根，不使能殖。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant, relying on the majesty of Great Han, has devised a long-term strategy, wishing to cut off their root entirely so that they cannot multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant therefore draws upon the might of Han to pursue a lasting policy — to uproot the trouble at its source and leave it no room to spread.

sentences.zh: 本規三歲之費，用五十四億；

translations.literal: The original plan budgeted three years' expense at five hundred forty million.
translations.idiomatic: The plan as first drawn up called for five hundred forty million cash over three years.

sentences.zh: 今適期年，所耗未半，而餘寇殘燼，將向殄滅。

translations.literal: Now barely a full year has passed, less than half has been spent, and the remaining bandits are dying embers, about to be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scarcely a year has gone by, less than half the funds have been consumed, and the remnant rebels are little more than smoldering ash, on the verge of annihilation.

sentences.zh: 臣每奉詔書，軍不內御，願卒斯言，一以任臣，臨時量宜，不失權便。

translations.literal: Your servant, whenever receiving imperial edicts saying the army must not enter to defend, wishes to see this proposal carried through to completion — leave everything to your servant, who will measure affairs as the moment requires without failing in flexible expedience.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I receive an edict forbidding the army to march inward in defense, I beg that this plan be allowed to run its course — entrust the matter wholly to me, and I shall act as circumstances demand without losing sight of what is expedient.

sentences.zh: 」八月，司空王暢免，宗正劉寵為司空。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Minister of Works Wang Chang was dismissed; Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Chong was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wang Chang was removed from the post of Minister of Works, and Liu Chong, Director of the Imperial Clan, was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 初，竇太后之立也，陳蕃有力焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Dowager Dou was installed, Chen Fan had done much to bring it about.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Dou was first elevated, Chen Fan had played no small part in it.

sentences.zh: 及臨朝，政無大小，皆委於蕃。

translations.literal: When she took the reins of government, matters great and small were all entrusted to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Once she assumed the regency, she entrusted every affair, great or small, to Chen Fan.

sentences.zh: 蕃與竇武同心戮力，以獎王室，徵天下名賢李膺、杜宻、尹勳、劉瑜等，皆列於朝廷，與共參政事。

translations.literal: Fan and Dou Wu worked with one heart and shared purpose to support the royal house; they summoned renowned men from across the realm — Li Ying, Du Mi, Yin Xun, Liu Yu, and others — all placing them at court to jointly deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan and Dou Wu joined forces in a single-minded effort to restore the throne, summoning celebrated men from throughout the empire — Li Ying, Du Mi, Yin Xun, Liu Yu, and others — and seating them at court to share in the governance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是天下之士，莫不延頸想望太平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the scholars of the empire all craned their necks in hope, longing for peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent across the land craned their necks in anticipation, yearning for an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 而帝乳母趙嬈及諸女尚書，旦夕在太后側，中常侍曹節、王甫等共相朋結，諂事太后。

translations.literal: But the Emperor's wet nurse Zhao Rao and several female secretaries were at the Empress Dowager's side day and night; the Palace Attendants Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and others formed a mutual faction to flatter and serve the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Emperor's wet nurse Zhao Rao and certain female secretaries attended the Empress Dowager from morning till night, while the palace eunuchs Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and their ilk banded together in a clique to fawn upon her.

sentences.zh: 太后信之，數出詔命，有所封拜。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager trusted them and repeatedly issued edicts granting appointments and enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager placed her faith in them and repeatedly issued edicts conferring offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 蕃、武疾之，嘗共會朝堂，蕃私謂武曰：「曹節、王甫等，自先帝時操弄國權，濁亂海內，今不誅之，後必難圖。

translations.literal: Fan and Wu hated this. Once when they met together at court, Fan privately said to Wu: "Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and the like have manipulated state power since the previous Emperor's time and muddied the realm; if we do not execute them now, they will be difficult to deal with later."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan and Dou Wu loathed this state of affairs. On one occasion when they met at court, Fan took Wu aside and said, "Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and their kind have twisted the levers of power since the late Emperor's day and poisoned the realm. If we do not destroy them now, we shall find them impossible to remove later."

sentences.zh: 」武深然之。

translations.literal: Wu deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 蕃大喜，以手椎席而起。

translations.literal: Fan was greatly delighted and rose from his seat, striking the mat with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan was overjoyed and struck the mat with his hand as he rose to his feet.

sentences.zh: 武於是引同志尚書令尹勳等共定計策。

translations.literal: Wu then brought in like-minded men, including Grand Secretary Yin Xun, to devise a plan together.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu thereupon gathered his allies, including the Grand Secretary Yin Xun, to lay their plans together.

sentences.zh: 會有日食之變，蕃謂武曰：「昔蕭望之困一石顯，況今石顯數十輩乎！

translations.literal: There happened to be a solar eclipse. Fan said to Wu: "Long ago Xiao Wangzhi was brought low by a single Shi Xian — how much more so now, when there are dozens upon dozens of Shi Xians!"
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse occurred about this time. Chen Fan said to Dou Wu, "In the old days Xiao Wangzhi was undone by a single Shi Xian — and now there are dozens of them!"

sentences.zh: 蕃以八十之年，欲為將軍除害，今可因日食斥罷宦官，以塞天變。

translations.literal: Fan, at eighty years of age, wishes to remove this evil for the General; we may now use the eclipse to dismiss and purge the eunuchs, thereby appeasing Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: I am eighty years old, yet I would still clear this scourge away for you, General. We may seize upon the eclipse to dismiss and purge the eunuchs, and so answer Heaven's reproof."

sentences.zh: 」武乃白太后曰：「故事，黃門、常侍但當給事省內典門戶，主近署財物耳；

translations.literal: Wu then reported to the Empress Dowager: "By precedent, the Yellow Gate attendants and Palace Attendants should only serve within the palace, managing gates and household goods;"
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu then addressed the Empress Dowager: "By ancient precedent, the Yellow Gate and Palace Attendants were charged only with service inside the palace — keeping the gates and overseeing the household stores."

sentences.zh: 今乃使與政事，任重權，子弟布列，專為貪暴。

translations.literal: Yet now they have been made to participate in government affairs, bearing heavy authority; their sons and brothers are arrayed everywhere, devoted solely to greed and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have been given a hand in affairs of state, laden with weighty power. Their sons and brothers fill every post, and they devote themselves to nothing but greed and cruelty."

sentences.zh: 天下匈匈，正以此故，宜悉誅廢以清朝廷。

translations.literal: The realm is in uproar precisely because of this; they should all be executed and removed to cleanse the court.
translations.idiomatic: The realm seethes with unrest for this very reason. They should all be executed and cast out, that the court may be cleansed."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「漢元以來故事，世有宦官，但當誅其有罪者，豈可盡廢邪！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Since the time of Emperor Yuan of Han it has been precedent that each generation has eunuchs; only the guilty should be executed — how can they all be abolished!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager replied, "Since the reign of Emperor Yuan it has been the custom of every generation to keep eunuchs in service. Only the guilty should be punished — how could we abolish them altogether?"

sentences.zh: 」時中常侍管霸，頗有才略，專制省內，武先白收霸及中常侍蘇康等，皆坐死。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Attendant Guan Ba was rather talented in strategy and monopolized power within the palace; Wu first reported requesting the arrest of Ba and the Palace Attendant Su Kang and others, all of whom were executed for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Palace Attendant Guan Ba was a man of some ability who had seized control within the palace precincts. Dou Wu first memorialized for the arrest of Ba, the Palace Attendant Su Kang, and others; all were condemned and executed.

sentences.zh: 武復數白誅曹節等，太后□豫未忍，故事久不發。

translations.literal: Wu repeatedly reported requesting the execution of Cao Jie and others; the Empress Dowager hesitated and could not bear it, and the plan long went unimplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu repeatedly memorialized for the execution of Cao Jie and his faction, but the Empress Dowager hesitated and could not bring herself to act; the plan languished for a long time without being carried out.

sentences.zh: 蕃上疏曰：「今京師囂囂，道路喧嘩，言侯覽、曹節、公乘昕、王甫、鄭颯等，與趙夫人、諸尚書並亂天下，附從者升進，忤逆者中傷，一朝群臣如河中木耳，泛泛東西，耽祿畏害。

translations.literal: Fan submitted a memorial saying: "Now the capital clamors and the roads resound with talk that Hou Lan, Cao Jie, Gongcheng Xin, Wang Fu, Zheng Sa, and others together with Lady Zhao and various secretaries are throwing the realm into chaos — those who follow them are promoted, those who oppose them are slandered; the ministers of a morning are like fungus floating on a river, drifting east and west, clinging to their salaries and fearing harm."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan submitted a memorial stating, "The capital is in an uproar and the streets ring with reports that Hou Lan, Cao Jie, Gongcheng Xin, Wang Fu, Zheng Sa, and others, together with Lady Zhao and the secretaries, are throwing the realm into chaos. Those who attach themselves to them rise in rank; those who cross them are destroyed by slander. The ministers at court drift like fungus on a river, carried this way and that, clinging to their stipends and dreading retribution."

sentences.zh: 陛下今不急誅此曹，必生變亂，傾危社稷，其難量。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, if you do not swiftly execute this pack, rebellion will surely arise and the altars of state will be overturned — the disaster is beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not move swiftly to destroy this pack, calamity and revolt will surely follow, and the altars of state will be overturned — the consequences are beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 願出臣章宣示左右，並令天下諸奸知臣疾之。

translations.literal: I beg that my memorial be made public to those around you, and that all villains under Heaven may know how fiercely I oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this memorial be shown to those at your side, and that every villain in the realm may know the depth of my resolve against them."

sentences.zh: 」太后不納。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager refused to heed it.

sentences.zh: 是月，太白犯房之上將，入太微。

translations.literal: That month, the star Venus intruded upon the Upper General of the Room constellation and entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, the planet Venus trespassed against the Upper General star of the Room asterism and entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 侍中劉瑜素善天官，惡之，上書皇太后曰：「案《占書》：宮門當閉，將相不利，奸人在主傍，願急防之。

translations.literal: Attendant Within Liu Yu, who had long been skilled in celestial affairs, was alarmed by this and wrote to the Empress Dowager: "According to the Books of Prognostication: the palace gates ought to be shut; generals and ministers face misfortune; villains are at the sovereign's side — I beg you to guard against this urgently."
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant Within Liu Yu, who had long been versed in celestial matters, was deeply troubled and wrote to the Empress Dowager: "The Books of Prognostication declare that when the palace gates should be closed, generals and ministers face peril and villains stand at the sovereign's side. I beg Your Majesty to guard against this at once."

sentences.zh: 」又與武、蕃書，以星辰錯繆，不利大臣，宜速斷大計。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Wu and Fan that the stars were in disorder, unfavorable to great ministers, and that they should swiftly settle upon a decisive plan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Dou Wu and Chen Fan that the stars were awry and ill-omened for great ministers, and that they must settle upon a decisive course without delay.

sentences.zh: 於是武、蕃以朱寓為司隸校尉，劉祐為河南尹、虞祁為雒陽令。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu and Fan appointed Zhu Yu as Director of the Capital Protectorate, Liu You as Intendant of Henan, and Yu Qi as magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Dou Wu and Chen Fan appointed Zhu Yu Director of the Capital Protectorate, Liu You Intendant of Henan, and Yu Qi magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 武奏免黃門令魏彪，以所親小黃門山冰代之，使冰奏收長樂尚書鄭颯，送北寺獄。

translations.literal: Wu memorialized to dismiss the Yellow Gate Director Wei Biao, replacing him with his trusted Junior Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Bing; he had Bing memorialize to arrest Changle Secretary Zheng Sa and send him to the Northern Prison.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu memorialized for the dismissal of the Yellow Gate Director Wei Biao and replaced him with his own man, the Junior Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Bing. He then had Bing submit a memorial for the arrest of the Changle Secretary Zheng Sa and his transfer to the Northern Prison.

sentences.zh: 蕃謂武曰：「此曹子便當收殺，何復考為！

translations.literal: Fan said to Wu: "These creatures ought to be arrested and killed at once — why interrogate them further!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan said to Dou Wu, "These wretches should be seized and put to death immediately — why bother with interrogation!"

sentences.zh: 」武不從，令冰與尹勳、侍御史祝□雜考颯，辭連及曹節、王甫。

translations.literal: Wu did not agree and had Bing, together with Yin Xun and Imperial Censor Zhu Liang, jointly interrogate Sa; his confession implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu would not hear of it. He had Bing, together with Yin Xun and the Imperial Censor Zhu Liang, jointly examine Zheng Sa. Under questioning, Sa's testimony implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 勳、冰即奏收節等，使劉瑜內奏。

translations.literal: Yin Xun and Bing immediately memorialized to arrest Jie and others; Liu Yu was made to report inward.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xun and Bing at once memorialized for the arrest of Cao Jie and his associates, while Liu Yu was dispatched to deliver the report within the palace.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛亥，武出宿歸府。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day of the ninth month, Wu went out and lodged at his own residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai in the ninth month, Dou Wu left the palace and returned to lodge at his own residence.

sentences.zh: 典中書者先以告長樂五官史朱瑀，瑀盜發武奏，罵曰：「中官放縱者，自可誅耳，我曹何罪，而當盡見族滅！

translations.literal: Those in charge of the Secretariat first informed Changle Five Offices Clerk Zhu Yu; Yu secretly opened Wu's memorial and cursed: "Those among the palace officials who are licentious may be executed — but what crime have we committed that we should all be exterminated to the last clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who handled the Secretariat documents first alerted Zhu Yu, a clerk of the Changle Five Offices. Zhu Yu secretly opened Dou Wu's memorial and raged, "The corrupt among the palace staff may deserve death — but what crime have we committed, that we should all be wiped out to the last clan!"

sentences.zh: 」因大呼曰：「陳蕃、竇武奏白太后廢帝，為大逆！

translations.literal: He then cried out loudly: "Chen Fan and Dou Wu have memorialized the Empress Dowager to depose the Emperor — this is supreme treason!"
translations.idiomatic: He then shouted aloud, "Chen Fan and Dou Wu have memorialized the Empress Dowager to depose the Emperor — this is treason of the highest order!"

sentences.zh: 」乃夜召素所親壯健者長樂從官史共普、張亮等十七人，歃血共盟，謀誅武等。

translations.literal: That night he summoned seventeen stalwart followers he had long favored — Changle attendant clerks Gong Pu, Zhang Liang, and others — and they mingled blood in a covenant, plotting to kill Wu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: That night he summoned seventeen stalwart men he had long favored among the Changle attendants — Gong Pu, Zhang Liang, and others — and they swore a blood oath together, plotting the death of Dou Wu and his allies.

sentences.zh: 曹節白帝曰：「外間切切，請出御德陽前殿。

translations.literal: Cao Jie reported to the Emperor: "Outside there is urgent commotion — I beg Your Majesty to proceed to the front hall of Deyang."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie reported to the Emperor, "There is urgent alarm outside — I beg Your Majesty to withdraw to the front hall of Deyang Palace."

sentences.zh: 」令帝拔劍踴躍，使乳母趙嬈等擁衛左右，取棨信，閉諸禁門，召尚書官屬，脅以白刃，使作詔板，拜王甫為黃門令，持節至北寺獄，收尹勳、山冰。

translations.literal: He had the Emperor draw his sword and leap forth; Zhao Rao the wet nurse and others were made to surround and guard him on left and right; they took the tallies of authority, shut all forbidden gates, summoned the secretaries of the Masters of Writing, and compelled them at sword-point to draft an edict board appointing Wang Fu as Yellow Gate Director; Fu bore the staff of authority to the Northern Prison to arrest Yin Xun and Shan Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Emperor draw his sword and spring forward, while the wet nurse Zhao Rao and others closed ranks around him. They seized the tallies of authority, barred every inner gate, summoned the secretaries of the Masters of Writing, and forced them at blade-point to draft an edict appointing Wang Fu Yellow Gate Director. Wang Fu then took the imperial staff to the Northern Prison to arrest Yin Xun and Shan Bing.

sentences.zh: 冰疑，不受詔，甫格殺之，並殺勳；

translations.literal: Bing was suspicious and refused the edict; Fu struck him down and killed him, and killed Xun as well;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Bing grew suspicious and refused to accept the edict. Wang Fu struck him down on the spot and killed him, and Yin Xun was slain as well.

sentences.zh: 出鄭颯，還兵劫太后，奪璽綬。

translations.literal: They released Zheng Sa, then returned with troops to seize the Empress Dowager, wresting away her seal and cord of office.
translations.idiomatic: They released Zheng Sa, then turned their troops upon the Empress Dowager, seizing her by force and stripping her of the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 令中謁者守南宮，閉門絕復道。

translations.literal: They ordered Palace Ushers to guard the Southern Palace, shut the gates, and cut off the covered passage.
translations.idiomatic: They posted palace ushers to hold the Southern Palace, barred the gates, and severed the covered passageway.

sentences.zh: 使鄭颯等持節及侍御史謁者捕收武等。

translations.literal: They sent Zheng Sa and others bearing staffs of authority, along with attendants-cum-imperial censors, to arrest Wu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched Zheng Sa and others, bearing the imperial staff, together with attendant-censors, to seize Dou Wu and his party.

sentences.zh: 武不受詔，馳入步兵營，與其兄子步兵校尉紹共射殺使者。

translations.literal: Wu refused the edict, galloped into the Infantry Camp, and together with his elder brother's son Shao, Colonel of the Infantry, jointly shot and killed the emissaries.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu refused the edict, galloped into the Infantry Camp, and together with his nephew Shao, Colonel of the Infantry, shot down the envoys.

sentences.zh: 召會北軍五校士數千人屯都亭，下令軍士曰：「黃門、常侍反，盡力者封侯重賞。

translations.literal: He mustered several thousand soldiers from the five colonels of the Northern Army and encamped them at Duting, issuing orders to the troops: "The Yellow Gate attendants and Palace Attendants have rebelled — those who give their utmost will be enfeoffed as marquises and richly rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: He rallied several thousand men from the five colonels of the Northern Army and encamped them at Duting, proclaiming to the troops, "The Yellow Gate and Palace Attendants have risen in rebellion! Those who fight with all their strength shall be enfeoffed as marquises and richly rewarded."

sentences.zh: 」陳蕃聞難，將官屬諸生八十餘人，並拔刃突入承明門，到尚書門，攘臂呼曰：「大將軍忠以衛國，黃門反逆，何-{云}-竇氏不道邪！

translations.literal: Chen Fan, hearing of the crisis, led more than eighty officials and students, all drawing blades as they burst through Chenming Gate; reaching the gate of the Masters of Writing, he rolled up his sleeves and cried: "The Grand General has been loyal in guarding the state — the Yellow Gate has rebelled in treason — how can you say the Dou clan is without the Way!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan heard of the crisis, he led more than eighty officials and students, blades drawn, and forced their way through Chenming Gate. Reaching the gate of the Masters of Writing, he rolled up his sleeves and shouted, "The Grand General has served the realm in loyalty — it is the Yellow Gate that has rebelled! How can you say the House of Dou is in the wrong!"

sentences.zh: 」王甫時出與蕃相遇，適聞其言，而讓蕃曰：「先帝新棄天下，山陵未成，武有何功，兄弟父子並封三侯！

translations.literal: Wang Fu happened to emerge and meet Fan just then; hearing his words, he reproached Fan: "The former Emperor has but newly departed this world and his tomb mound is not yet complete — what merit has Wu, that brothers, fathers, and sons should all be enfeoffed as three marquises!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu happened to come out just then and encounter Chen Fan. Hearing these words, he turned on him and said, "The late Emperor has scarcely left this world, and his tomb is not yet finished — by what merit has Dou Wu earned three marquisates for brothers, fathers, and sons alike!"

sentences.zh: 又設樂飲宴，多取掖廷宮人，旬日之間，貲財巨萬，大臣若此，為是道邪！

translations.literal: And he holds feasts with music, taking many palace women from the Inner Household — within ten days his wealth reached tens of thousands! If a great minister behaves thus, is this the Way!
translations.idiomatic: He holds feasts with music, seizing palace women from the Inner Household by the score — and within ten days his wealth swelled to tens of thousands! Is this how a great minister ought to conduct himself? Is this the Way?"

sentences.zh: 公為宰輔，苟相阿黨，復何求賊！

translations.literal: You are chief ministers; if you mutually flatter and form factions, what more need we do to find the villains!
translations.idiomatic: You stand at the head of the realm—yet if you only flatter one another and band together, what further search need we make for the true villains?

sentences.zh: 」使劍士收蕃，蕃拔劍叱甫，辭色逾厲。
