translations.literal: " Swordsmen were sent to seize Fan; Fan drew his sword and shouted at Fu, his words and expression growing ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Swordsmen were dispatched to take Chen Fan. Fan drew his blade and shouted down Wang Fu, his voice and bearing turning ever harsher.

sentences.zh: 遂執蕃，送北寺獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon they seized Fan and sent him to the Northern Prison.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Fan at once and had him conveyed to the Northern Prison.

sentences.zh: 黃門從官騶蹋踧蕃曰：「死老魅！

translations.literal: Yellow Gate attendants and runners trampled on Fan, saying: "Dead old demon!
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate attendants and runners trampled him, crying, "You dead old fiend!

sentences.zh: 復能損我曹員數、奪我曹稟假不！

translations.literal: Can you still reduce our numbers and take away our salaries and allowances or not!
translations.idiomatic: Can you still cut our ranks and strip us of our stipends and perquisites, can you?"

sentences.zh: 」即日，殺之。

translations.literal: " That same day, they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: That very day they put him to death.

sentences.zh: 時護匈奴中郎將張奐徵還京師，曹節等以奐新至，不知本謀，矯制以少府周靖行車騎將軍、加節，與奐率五營士討武。

translations.literal: At the time Protector of the Xiongnu Zhonglang General Zhang Huan was recalled to the capital; Cao Jie and others, because Huan had just arrived and did not know the original plot, forged an edict appointing Director of Palace Privy Supplies Zhou Jing acting General of Chariots and Cavalry with staff of office, to join Huan in leading the Five Camp soldiers to attack Dou Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Xiongnu Zhonglang General Zhang Huan had just been summoned back to the capital. Cao Jie and his faction, knowing Huan was newly arrived and ignorant of their design, forged an imperial order making Palace Privy Director Zhou Jing acting General of Chariots and Cavalry with full credentials, to march with Huan at the head of the Five Camp troops against Dou Wu.

sentences.zh: 夜漏盡，王甫將虎賁、羽林等合千餘人，出屯朱雀掖門，與奐等合，已而悉軍闕下，與武對陳。

translations.literal: When the night watch ended, Wang Fu led the Tiger Guards and Feathered Forest Guard, over a thousand men in all, out to encamp at the Vermilion Bird side gate; he joined Huan and the others, then massed the whole force below the palace gates and drew up in battle array facing Dou Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the night watch Wang Fu led more than a thousand Tiger Guard and Feathered Forest troops out to hold the Vermilion Bird side gate. He joined Zhang Huan's force, then drew the entire army up beneath the palace gates and formed ranks opposite Dou Wu.

sentences.zh: 甫兵漸盛，使其士大呼武軍曰：「竇武反，汝皆禁兵，當宿衛宮省，何故隨反者乎！

translations.literal: Fu's forces gradually grew stronger; he had his soldiers shout loudly to Dou Wu's army: "Dou Wu has rebelled! You are all imperial guard soldiers who should guard the palace precincts—why do you follow rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu's numbers steadily swelled. He had his men shout across to Dou Wu's host: "Dou Wu has risen in rebellion! You are palace guards, sworn to keep watch over the inner precincts—why do you march with a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 先降有賞！

translations.literal: Those who surrender first will be rewarded!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever yields first shall be rewarded!"

sentences.zh: 」營府兵素畏服中官，於是武軍稍稍歸甫，自旦至食時，兵降略盡。

translations.literal: " The camp soldiers had always feared and submitted to the eunuchs; thus Dou Wu's army gradually went over to Fu, and from dawn until mealtime the soldiers nearly all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison troops had long feared and obeyed the eunuchs. Dou Wu's lines began to melt away toward Wang Fu, and from dawn until the morning meal nearly the whole force had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 武、紹走，諸軍追圍之，皆自殺，梟首雒陽都亭；

translations.literal: Dou Wu and Shao fled; the various armies pursued and surrounded them; both committed suicide, and their heads were displayed at the Luoyang capital pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu and Dou Shao fled. Pursuing columns closed in on them from every side. Both took their own lives, and their heads were hung at the Luoyang capital pavilion.

sentences.zh: 收捕宗親賓客姻屬，悉誅之，及侍中劉瑜、屯騎校尉馮述，皆夷其族。

translations.literal: They arrested kinsmen, retainers, guests, and relatives by marriage and executed them all; Palace Attendant Liu Yu and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Feng Shu were also implicated, and their entire clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen, clients, guests, and in-laws were hunted down and put to death without exception. Palace Attendant Liu Yu and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Feng Shu were swept up as well, and their whole clans were annihilated.

sentences.zh: 宦官又譖虎賁中郎將河間劉淑、故尚書會稽魏朗，-{云}-與武等通謀，皆自殺。

translations.literal: The eunuchs also slandered Tiger Guard Zhonglang General Liu Shu of Hejian and former Master of Writing Wei Lang of Kuaiji, saying they had conspired with Dou Wu and the others; all committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs also denounced Tiger Guard Zhonglang General Liu Shu of Hejian and former Master of Writing Wei Lang of Kuaiji, claiming they had plotted with Dou Wu and his allies. Both men killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 遷皇太后於南宮，徙武家屬於日南；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was moved to the Southern Palace; Dou Wu's family members were exiled to Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was removed to the Southern Palace, and Dou Wu's household was banished to Rinan.

sentences.zh: 自公卿以下嘗為蕃、武所舉者及門生故吏，皆免官禁錮。

translations.literal: From the Three Ducal Ministers downward, all who had been recommended by Fan and Wu, as well as their disciples and former subordinates, were dismissed from office and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Every official from the Three Ducal Ministers down who had been promoted by Chen Fan or Dou Wu, together with their disciples and former retainers, was stripped of office and placed under detention.

sentences.zh: 議郎勃海巴肅，始與武等同謀，曹節等不知，但坐禁錮，後乃知而收之。

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Ba Su of Bohai had originally plotted together with Dou Wu and the others; Cao Jie and the others did not know this at first and only punished him with imprisonment; later, when they learned of it, they had him arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Consultant Ba Su of Bohai had taken part in the original plot with Dou Wu and his circle. Cao Jie and the rest did not know this at first and merely confined him; only later, when they discovered the truth, did they move to seize him.

sentences.zh: 肅自載詣縣，縣令見肅，入閣，解印綬，欲與俱去。

translations.literal: Su himself drove a cart to the county; when the county magistrate saw Su, he entered his private chamber, removed his seal and sash, and intended to flee together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Su drove himself to the county seat. When the magistrate saw him coming, he withdrew to his inner chamber, took off his seal and sash, and prepared to flee with him.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「為人臣者，有謀不敢隱，有罪不逃刑，既不隱其謀矣，又敢逃其刑乎！

translations.literal: Su said: "As a subject, when one has a plot one dare not conceal it; when one has guilt one does not flee punishment. Since I have not concealed my plot, how dare I now flee my punishment!
translations.idiomatic: Ba Su said, "A loyal subject who has taken part in a plot does not hide it; one who has committed a crime does not run from judgment. I did not conceal my part in the plot—how then could I flee the penalty?"

sentences.zh: 」遂被誅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed.

sentences.zh: 曹節遷長樂衛尉，封育陽侯。

translations.literal: Cao Jie was transferred to Commandant of Changle Palace Guards and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie was made Commandant of the Changle Palace Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 王甫遷中常侍，黃門令如故。

translations.literal: Wang Fu was transferred to Regular Palace Attendant; his post as Yellow Gate Prefect remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant while retaining his office as Yellow Gate Prefect.

sentences.zh: 朱瑀、共普、張亮等六人皆為列侯，十一人為關內侯。

translations.literal: Zhu Yu, Gong Pu, Zhang Liang, and six others all became full marquises; eleven men became Marquises Within the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu, Gong Pu, Zhang Liang, and five others were all made full marquises; eleven more were raised to Marquises Within the Pass.

sentences.zh: 於是群小得志，士大夫皆喪氣。

translations.literal: Thus the petty men had their way, and the scholar-officials all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men now had their heart's desire, and the scholar-officials sank into despair.

sentences.zh: 蕃友人陳留朱震收葬蕃屍，匿其子逸，事覺，繫獄，合門桎梏。

translations.literal: Fan's friend Zhu Zhen of Chenliu collected and buried Fan's corpse and hid his son Yi; when the matter was discovered, he was imprisoned and the whole household put in shackles.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan's friend Zhu Zhen of Chenliu gathered up Fan's body for burial and hid his son Yi. When the affair came to light, Zhu was thrown into prison and his entire household clapped in irons.

sentences.zh: 震受拷掠，誓死不言，逸由是得免。

translations.literal: Zhen endured torture and beating, swearing to die rather than speak; Yi was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen endured torture and flogging, vowing to die rather than speak—and Yi was spared.

sentences.zh: 武府掾桂陽胡騰殯斂武屍，行喪，坐以禁錮。

translations.literal: Dou Wu's bureau aide Hu Teng of Guiyang prepared and buried Dou Wu's corpse and observed mourning rites; he was punished with imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu's staff officer Hu Teng of Guiyang laid out and buried Dou Wu's body and performed the mourning rites. For this he was sentenced to detention.

sentences.zh: 武孫輔，年二歲，騰詐以為己子，與令史南陽張敞共匿之於零陵界中，亦得免。

translations.literal: Dou Wu's grandson Fu, two years old—Teng falsely claimed him as his own son and, together with clerk Zhang Chang of Nanyang, hid him within the Lingling borderlands; he too was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu's grandson Fu was only two years old. Hu Teng passed him off as his own child and, with clerk Zhang Chang of Nanyang, concealed him in the wilds near Lingling. The boy too survived.

sentences.zh: 張奐遷大司農，以功封侯。

translations.literal: Zhang Huan was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as marquis for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as marquis for his service.

sentences.zh: 奐深病為曹節等所賣，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Huan deeply resented being used by Cao Jie and the others and steadfastly refused to accept the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was deeply shamed at having been made the eunuchs' instrument and firmly refused the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 以司徒胡廣為太傅，錄尚書事，司空劉寵為司徒，大鴻臚許栩為司空。

translations.literal: Hu Guang, Grand Commandant, was made Grand Tutor with charge of the Secretariat; Liu Chong, Minister of Works, became Grand Commandant; Xu Xu, Grand Herald, became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Hu Guang was made Grand Tutor with oversight of the Secretariat; Minister of Works Liu Chong became Grand Commandant; Grand Herald Xu Xu became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the last day of the jia-chen cycle, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the last day of the cycle, jia-chen, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，太尉劉矩免，以太僕沛國聞人襲為太尉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Grand Marshal Liu Ju was dismissed; Wenren Xi of Pei, Director of Imperial Transport, was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Grand Marshal Liu Ju was removed from office, and Wenren Xi of Pei, Director of the Imperial Transport, was appointed Grand Marshal in his place.

sentences.zh: 十二月，鮮卑及濊貊寇幽、并二州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Xianbei and Wuhuan raided You and Bing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Xianbei and Wuhuan struck at You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 是歲，疏勒王季父和得殺其王自立。

translations.literal: That year, the king's uncle Hede of Shule killed the king and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hede, the king's uncle in Shule, murdered the reigning king and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 烏桓大人上谷難樓有眾九千餘落，遼西丘力居有眾五千餘落，自稱王。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan chieftain Nalou of Shanggu had over nine thousand households; Qiuliju of Liaoxi had over five thousand households; both proclaimed themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Wuhuan, Nalou of Shanggu commanded more than nine thousand households, and Qiuliju of Liaoxi more than five thousand; each declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 遼東蘇僕延有眾千餘落，自稱峭王。

translations.literal: Supuyan of Liaodong had over a thousand households and proclaimed himself Qiao King.
translations.idiomatic: Supuyan of Liaodong mustered more than a thousand households and styled himself King Qiao.

sentences.zh: 右北平烏延有眾八百餘落，自稱汗魯王。

translations.literal: Wuyan of Youbeiping had over eight hundred households and proclaimed himself Hanlu King.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan of Youbeiping gathered more than eight hundred households and called himself King Hanlu.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁丑，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on ding-chou day, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on ding-chou, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝迎董貴人於河間。

translations.literal: The Emperor welcomed Lady Dong from Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brought Lady Dong from Hejian into the palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙巳，尊為孝仁皇后，居永樂宮，拜其兄寵為執金吾，兄子重為五官中郎將。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yi-si day, she was honored as Empress Xiaoren, residing in Yongle Palace; her elder brother Chong was appointed Commandant of the Capital Guard, and her brother's son Zhong was appointed Five-Office Zhonglang General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yi-si, she was elevated as Empress Xiaoren and installed in Yongle Palace. Her elder brother Chong was made Commandant of the Capital Guard, and her nephew Zhong Five-Office Zhonglang General.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬辰，有青蛇見於御坐上。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on ren-chen day, a green serpent appeared on the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on ren-chen, a green serpent was seen coiled upon the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大風，雨雹，霹靂，拔大木百餘。

translations.literal: On gui-si day, there was great wind, hail, and thunder; over a hundred large trees were uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: On gui-si a great wind rose, hail fell, and thunder cracked the sky; more than a hundred great trees were torn up by the roots.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿以下各上封事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all from the Three Ducal Ministers downward to submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out commanding every official from the Three Ducal Ministers down to submit sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 大司農張奐上疏曰：「昔周公葬不如禮，天乃動威。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Huan submitted a memorial saying: "In former times, when the Duke of Zhou's burial did not conform to ritual, Heaven moved to show its wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Huan memorialized the throne: "Long ago, when the Duke of Zhou was buried without proper rites, Heaven itself stirred in anger.

sentences.zh: 今竇武、陳蕃忠貞，未被明宥，妖眚之來，皆為此也。

translations.literal: Now Dou Wu and Chen Fan were loyal and steadfast, yet have not received clear pardon; the coming of portents and calamities is all on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu and Chen Fan were men of loyalty and integrity, yet they have never been openly cleared. The strange omens that have followed all spring from this wrong.

sentences.zh: 宜急為改葬，徙還家屬，其從坐禁錮，一切蠲除。

translations.literal: It is fitting urgently to re-inter them properly, return their families, and completely remit all who were implicated and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should at once grant them honorable reburial, restore their families, and release every person implicated and held in detention.

sentences.zh: 又，皇太后雖居南宮，而恩禮不接，朝臣莫言，遠近失望。

translations.literal: Moreover, though the Empress Dowager resides in the Southern Palace, grace and ritual courtesies are not extended to her; court ministers dare not speak, and near and far alike are disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the Empress Dowager dwells in the Southern Palace, no grace or proper ceremony reaches her. The court dares not speak of it, and men near and far have lost hope.

sentences.zh: 宜思大義顧復之報。

translations.literal: One ought to reflect upon the great principle and repay her nurturing kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should weigh the greater duty and repay the kindness of the mother who raised you.

sentences.zh: 」上深嘉奐言，以問諸常侍，左右皆惡之，帝不得自從。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved Huan's words and asked the various regular attendants about it; those around him all detested the proposal, and the Emperor could not act on his own inclination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved by Zhang Huan's words and put the matter to his regular attendants—but every voice at his side turned against it, and he could not follow his own mind.

sentences.zh: 奐又與尚書劉猛等共薦王暢、李膺可參三公之選，曹節等彌疾其言，遂下詔切責之。

translations.literal: Huan again joined Masters of Writing Liu Meng and others in jointly recommending Wang Chang and Li Ying as fit to be considered for selection among the Three Excellencies; Cao Jie and his faction hated this talk all the more, and so an edict was issued sternly rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan again joined Master of Writing Liu Meng and others in recommending Wang Chang and Li Ying for the Three Excellencies. Cao Jie and his cohort were all the more furious, and an edict was issued sharply rebuking them.

sentences.zh: 奐等皆自囚廷尉，數日，乃得出，並以三月俸贖罪。

translations.literal: Huan and the others all voluntarily imprisoned themselves with the Director of Convicts; after several days they were finally released, and each paid three months' salary to redeem the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan and the others voluntarily turned themselves in to the Director of Convicts. After several days they were released, each forfeiting three months' salary to expiate the offense.

sentences.zh: 郎中東郡謝弼上封事曰：「臣聞『惟虺惟蛇，女子之祥』。

translations.literal: Xie Bi, a palace gentleman from Dong Commandery, submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard, 'Only the viper, only the snake—a woman's omen.'
translations.idiomatic: Xie Bi, a palace gentleman from Dong Commandery, submitted a sealed memorial: "I have heard it said: 'Only the viper, only the snake—the omen of a woman.'"

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太后定策宮闥，援立聖明，《書》曰：『父子兄弟，罪不相及』，竇氏之誅，豈宜咎延太后！

translations.literal: Bowing low, I consider that the Empress Dowager fixed the policy within the palace gates and helped enthrone the sage and enlightened ruler. The Documents says: 'Between father and son, elder and younger brother, guilt does not extend to one another.' The execution of the Dou clan—how can blame properly extend to the Empress Dowager!
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that the Empress Dowager settled the succession within the palace and set a wise ruler upon the throne. The Book of Documents says: "Between fathers and sons, brothers—guilt does not reach across kin." The Dou clan was destroyed—how can that blame be laid upon the Empress Dowager!

sentences.zh: 幽隔空宮，愁感天心，如有霧露之疾，陛下當何面目以見天下！

translations.literal: Sequestered in an empty palace, her sorrow moves Heaven's heart, as though suffering an illness of mist and dew—how can Your Majesty show what face to meet all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: She dwells alone in an empty palace, her grief stirring Heaven itself, like one wasting away with a lingering illness—what face can Your Majesty show to the empire!

sentences.zh: 孝和皇帝不絕竇氏之恩，前世以為美談。

translations.literal: Emperor He of Xia never cut off kindness toward the Dou clan—a matter the previous age took as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He never broke with the Dou clan, and the age held that up as a noble example.

sentences.zh: 禮，『為人後者為之子』，今以桓帝為父，豈得不以太后為母哉！

translations.literal: In ritual, 'one who becomes the heir becomes as a son'; now that Emperor Huan is taken as son, how can he fail to take the Empress Dowager as mother!
translations.idiomatic: Ritual says: "He who becomes another's heir stands as a son." Emperor Huan was made heir to the throne—how can he not treat the Empress Dowager as his mother!

sentences.zh: 願陛下仰慕有虞蒸蒸之化，俯思《凱風》慰母之念。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty look up to the transforming virtue of Youyu's warmth, and bend your thoughts to the Ode to the South Wind's comfort for a mother's longing.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty look up to the gentle warmth of the age of Shun, and bend your mind to the Ode to the South Wind and its longing to comfort a mother.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞『開國承家，小人勿用』。

translations.literal: Your servant further hears, 'In founding a state and inheriting a household, petty men are not to be employed.'
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: "In founding a state and sustaining a house, do not employ petty men."

sentences.zh: 今功臣久外，未蒙爵秩，阿母寵私，乃享大封，大風雨雹，亦由於茲。

translations.literal: Now meritorious ministers long kept outside have not been granted titles and ranks; foster mothers favored in private intimacy enjoy great enfeoffments—the great wind, rain, and hail also stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers are kept at arm's length without titles or rank, while wet nurses favored in private enjoy great fiefs—the violent storms and hail owe to this as well.

sentences.zh: 又，故太傅陳蕃，勤身王室，而見陷群邪，一旦誅滅，其為酷濫，駭動天下；

translations.literal: Further, the late Grand Tutor Chen Fan devoted his person to the royal house, yet was entrapped by a pack of wicked men and in a single day executed and wiped out—how cruel and excessive; it shocked and moved all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Again: the late Grand Tutor Chen Fan gave his life to the throne, yet was ensnared by wicked men and in a single stroke destroyed. The cruelty of it shook the empire;

sentences.zh: 而門生故吏，並離徙錮。

translations.literal: and his students and former subordinates were all exiled and banished with prohibition from office.
translations.idiomatic: his students and former subordinates were all exiled and barred from office.

sentences.zh: 蕃身已往，人百何贖！

translations.literal: Fan's person has already passed—when a hundred men live on, what can redeem it!
translations.idiomatic: Fan is dead—what can the living do to redeem him!

sentences.zh: 宜還其家屬，解除禁網，夫台宰重器，國命所繫，今之四公，唯司空劉寵斷斷守善，餘皆素餐致寇之人，必有折足覆餗之凶，可因災異，並加罷黜，征故司空王暢、長樂少府李膺並居政事，庶災變可消，國祚惟永。

translations.literal: It is fitting to return their families, lift the net of prohibitions; the minister-chancellor is a heavy vessel upon which the fate of the state depends. Of the four high ministers today, only Minister of Works Liu Chong steadfastly holds to goodness; the rest are all men who eat their salaries idle and bring calamity upon the realm—surely there will be the ill omen of a broken leg overturning the stew. One may use the calamities and anomalies as occasion to dismiss them all from office, summon the former Minister of Works Wang Chang and Chamberlain for the Palace of Changle Li Ying to share in governance together—in which case the calamitous changes may be dispelled and the dynasty's fortune made lasting.
translations.idiomatic: Restore their families and lift the ban. The chief ministers are the state's great anchors; upon them the realm's fate hangs. Of the four high ministers now, only Minister of Works Liu Chong holds fast to integrity; the rest feast on empty salaries and invite disaster—the omen of the broken leg and overturned feast cannot be far off. Use these portents to remove them all, recall former Minister of Works Wang Chang and Chamberlain for Changle Li Ying to govern—and the calamities may abate and the dynasty endure.

sentences.zh: 」左右惡其言，出為廣陵府丞，去官，歸家。

translations.literal: Those close at hand hated his words; he was sent out as assistant in the office of the Grand Administrator of Guangling, resigned office, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the throne hated what he said. He was posted as assistant to the grand administrator of Guangling, resigned his post, and went home.

sentences.zh: 曹節從子紹為東郡太守，以它罪收弼，掠死於獄。

translations.literal: Cao Jie's nephew Shao was Grand Administrator of Dong Commandery; on another charge he arrested Bi, who died under torture in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie's nephew Shao, grand administrator of Dong Commandery, had Bi arrested on another charge and tortured to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 帝以蛇妖問光祿勳楊賜，賜上封事曰：「夫善不妄來，災不空發。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yang Ci about the snake apparition; Ci submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Good does not come without cause; calamity does not arise in vain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yang Ci about the serpent omen. Ci submitted a sealed memorial: "Blessings do not arrive without cause, nor disasters without warning.

sentences.zh: 王者心有所想，雖未形顏色，而五星以之推移，陰陽為其變度。

translations.literal: When a king's heart harbors some thought, though it has not yet taken shape on the countenance, the five planets shift because of it, and yin and yang alter their measures for it.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's heart holds a thought, even before it shows on his face, the five planets shift and yin and yang alter their courses.

sentences.zh: 夫皇極不建，則有龍蛇之孽，《詩》云：『惟虺惟蛇，女子之祥。

translations.literal: When the sovereign pole is not established, then come the portents of dragons and snakes. The Odes say: 'Only the viper, only the snake—a woman's omen.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal pole is unsettled, serpent portents appear. The Odes say: "Only the viper, only the snake—the omen of a woman."

sentences.zh: 』惟陛下思乾剛之道，別內外之宜，抑皇甫之權，割艷妻之愛，則蛇變可消，禎祥立應。

translations.literal: '" Only may Your Majesty ponder the way of qian's firmness, distinguish inner and outer as proper, restrain Huangfu's power, and sever love for the beautiful wife—then the snake transformation may be dispelled and auspicious signs will quickly respond.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty hold to the firm way of Heaven, keep inner and outer in their proper places, restrain the Huangfu faction's power, and cut away fondness for a beautiful consort—then the serpent omen will fade and blessings will follow."

sentences.zh: 」賜，秉之子也。

translations.literal: " Ci was the son of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Ci was the son of Yang Bing.

sentences.zh: 五月，太尉聞人襲、司空許栩免；

translations.literal: Fifth month, Grand Commandant Wenren Xi and Minister of Works Xu Xu were dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Grand Commandant Wenren Xi and Minister of Works Xu Xu were removed from office;

sentences.zh: 六月，以司徒劉寵為太尉，太常汝南許訓為司徒，太僕長沙劉囂為司空。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Minister over the Masses Liu Chong was made Grand Commandant; Grand Master of Ceremonies Xu Xun of Runan was made Minister over the Masses; Grand Master of the Stud Liu Xiao of Changsha was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Chong, Minister over the Masses, was appointed Grand Commandant; Xu Xun of Runan, Grand Master of Ceremonies, became Minister over the Masses; and Liu Xiao of Changsha, Grand Master of the Stud, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 囂素附諸常侍，故致位公輔。

translations.literal: Xiao had long attached himself to the various palace attendants, and for this reason reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiao had long curried favor with the eunuch attendants, and that was how he rose to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 詔遣謁者馮禪說降漢陽散羌。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Internuncio Feng Chan to persuade the scattered Qiang of Hanyang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Internuncio Feng Chan to win the surrender of the scattered Qiang in Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 段熲以春農，百姓布野，羌雖暫降，而縣官無廩，必當復為盜賊，不如乘虛放兵，勢必殄滅。

translations.literal: Duan Yong, considering that it was spring and farmers were spread across the fields, though the Qiang had temporarily surrendered, the district offices had no granaries—they would surely become bandits again—it would be better to seize the moment of emptiness and release troops; the momentum would surely exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong reasoned that with spring planting underway and farmers scattered across the fields, the Qiang might submit for the moment, but with no government granaries to feed them they would soon turn bandit again. Better to strike while they were exposed—troops released now would surely wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 熲於是自進營，去羌所屯凡亭山四五十里，遣騎司馬田晏、假司馬夏育將五千人先進，擊破之。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon advanced camp himself, forty or fifty li from where the Qiang were encamped at Fanting Mountain; he dispatched Cavalry Major Tian Yan and Acting Major Xia Yu to lead five thousand men in advance and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong advanced his camp to within forty or fifty li of the Qiang encampment at Fanting Mountain and sent Cavalry Major Tian Yan and Acting Major Xia Yu ahead with five thousand men to break them.

sentences.zh: 羌眾潰東奔，復聚射虎谷，分兵守谷上下門，熲規一舉滅之，不欲復令散走。

translations.literal: The Qiang host broke and fled east, then gathered again at Shehu Valley, dividing troops to guard the upper and lower gates of the valley; Yong planned to destroy them in one stroke and did not wish to let them scatter and flee again.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang broke and fled east, regrouping at Shehu Valley and posting troops at the upper and lower passes. Yong planned to finish them in one blow and would not let them scatter again.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，熲遣千人於西縣結木為柵，廣二十步，長四十里遮之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Yong dispatched a thousand men at Xi County to bind wood into a palisade twenty paces wide and forty li long to block them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yong had a thousand men at Xi County build a wooden palisade twenty paces wide and forty li long to block their escape.

sentences.zh: 分遣晏、育等將七千人銜枚夜上西山，結營穿塹，去虜一里許，又遣司馬張愷等將三千人上東山，虜乃覺之。

translations.literal: He separately dispatched Yan, Yu, and others with seven thousand men, holding sticks in their mouths, to mount West Mountain by night, encamp, and dig trenches about one li from the enemy; he also sent Major Zhang Kai and others with three thousand men up East Mountain—the enemy then discovered them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yan and Yu with seven thousand men, mouths gagged with wooden pegs, up West Mountain by night to camp and dig trenches a li from the enemy. Major Zhang Kai led three thousand up East Mountain—and only then did the Qiang notice.

sentences.zh: 熲因與愷等夾東、西山，縱兵奮擊，破之，追至谷上下門，窮山深谷之中，處處破之，斬其渠帥以下萬九千級。

translations.literal: Yong then, together with Kai and others, pinched them between East and West mountains, released troops in fierce assault, broke them, pursued to the upper and lower gates of the valley, and in steep mountains and deep ravines broke them everywhere, beheading nineteen thousand from chieftains downward.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Kai pressed the attack from both mountains, routed the Qiang, and pursued them to the valley gates—through mountain fastnesses and deep ravines, breaking them everywhere—taking nineteen thousand heads from chieftains down to the rank and file.

sentences.zh: 馮禪等所招降四千人，分置安定、漢陽、隴西三郡。

translations.literal: The four thousand whom Feng Chan and others had summoned to surrender were distributed and settled in the three commanderies of Anding, Hanyang, and Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand Qiang whom Feng Chan had won over were settled across Anding, Hanyang, and Longxi commanderies.

sentences.zh: 於是東羌悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Qiang were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Qiang were pacified at last.

sentences.zh: 熲凡百八十戰，斬三萬八千餘級，獲雜畜四十二萬七千餘頭，費用四十四億，軍士死者四百餘人；

translations.literal: Yong fought altogether one hundred eighty battles, beheaded more than thirty-eight thousand, captured more than four hundred twenty-seven thousand head of mixed livestock, expended four billion four hundred million in cost, and four hundred-odd soldiers died;
translations.idiomatic: In all Yong fought one hundred eighty engagements, took more than thirty-eight thousand heads, seized more than four hundred twenty-seven thousand head of livestock, spent four hundred forty million cash, and lost just over four hundred soldiers;

sentences.zh: 更封新豐縣侯，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinfeng District, fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Marquis of Xinfeng, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：書稱：「天地，萬物父母，惟人萬物之靈。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The Documents say: "Heaven and Earth are the parents of the ten thousand things; only man is the spirit of the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang comments: The Book of Documents says: "Heaven and Earth are the parents of all things; of all things, man alone is the spirit endowed."

sentences.zh: 但聰明，作元-{后}-，元-{后}-作民父母。

translations.literal: Let the intelligent and enlightened be made the primary sovereign, and the primary sovereign be made the people's parents."
translations.idiomatic: Let the wise and enlightened become sovereign, and the sovereign become the people's parents."

sentences.zh: 」夫蠻夷戎狄，氣類雖殊，其就利避害，樂生惡死，亦與人同耳。

translations.literal: Now the Man, Yi, Rong, and Di—though their qi and kind differ, in seeking advantage and avoiding harm, delighting in life and hating death, they are the same as men.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian tribes of the four directions differ in nature, yet in seeking gain and fleeing harm, in loving life and fearing death, they are no different from us.

sentences.zh: 御之得其道則附順服從，失其道則離叛侵擾，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Governing them by obtaining the right Way, they attach, submit, and obey; losing the Way, they split off, rebel, and harass—this is naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: Govern them rightly and they submit; govern them wrongly and they rebel and raid—that is only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 是以先王之政，叛則討之，服則懷之，處之四裔，不使亂禮義之邦而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the government of former kings: when they rebelled, they were punished; when they submitted, they were embraced with kindness; they were placed in the four borderlands and simply not allowed to disorder the domains of ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings punished rebellion and embraced submission, settling tribes on the outer marches so they would not disrupt the civilized realm—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 若乃視之如草木禽獸，不分臧否，不辨去來，悉艾殺之，豈作民父母之意哉！

translations.literal: If one treats them like grass, trees, birds, and beasts—not distinguishing good from bad, not distinguishing those who come from those who go, and slaughters them all with extirpation—is this the intent of being the people's parents!
translations.idiomatic: To treat them like weeds and wild beasts—to make no distinction between the loyal and the hostile, the departing and the staying—and slaughter them all: is that the mind of a ruler who would be the people's parent?

sentences.zh: 且夫羌之所以叛者，為郡縣所侵冤故也；

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason the Qiang rebel are because they are wronged and oppressed by the commanderies and districts;
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang rebel because commandery and county officials wrong them;

sentences.zh: 叛而不即誅者，將帥非其人故也。

translations.literal: when they rebel and are not immediately punished, it is because the generals and commanders are not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: when rebels go unpunished, it is because the wrong men hold command.

sentences.zh: 苟使良將驅而出之塞外，擇良吏而牧之，則疆場之臣也，豈得專以多殺為快邪！

translations.literal: If only one employs good generals to drive them out beyond the passes and selects good officials to shepherd them, they would be ministers of the frontier—how can one take pleasure solely in many killings!
translations.idiomatic: Send able generals to drive them beyond the frontier and appoint worthy officials to govern them, and they become guardians of the border—what joy is there in slaughter for its own sake!

sentences.zh: 夫御之不得其道，雖華夏之民，亦將蜂起而為寇，又可盡誅邪！

translations.literal: When governing without obtaining the right Way, even the people of the Central Plains would swarm up to become bandits—could one slay them all!
translations.idiomatic: Govern badly and even the people of the heartland will rise in rebellion—can you execute them all?

sentences.zh: 然則段紀明之為將，雖克捷有功，君子所不與也。

translations.literal: Thus Duan Jiming as a general—though he achieved victory and had merit—the gentleman does not accord with it.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiming won his battles and earned his laurels—but a gentleman will have no part of such methods.

sentences.zh: 九月，江夏蠻反，州郡討平之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Man barbarians of Jiangxia rebelled; the province and commanderies attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Man of Jiangxia rebelled; provincial and commandery forces put them down.

sentences.zh: 丹楊山越圍太守陳夤，夤擊破之。

translations.literal: The Shanyue of Danyang besieged Grand Administrator Chen Yin; Yin attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyue of Danyang besieged Grand Administrator Chen Yin; Yin drove them off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 初，李膺等雖廢錮，天下士大夫皆高尚其道而污穢朝廷，希之者唯恐不及，更共相標榜，為之稱號：以竇武、陳蕃、劉淑為三君，君者，言一世之所宗也；

translations.literal: Initially, though Li Ying and the others were barred from office, throughout the realm the scholar-officials all honored their Way and reviled the court; those who hoped to join them feared they could not catch up; they further mutually proclaimed one another and made titles for them: Dou Wu, Chen Fan, and Liu Shu were the Three Lords—'lord' meaning those the age looks up to as its models;
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Ying and his fellows had been barred from office, scholars everywhere honored their integrity and despised the court. Men vied to join them, outdoing one another in praise, and coined titles: Dou Wu, Chen Fan, and Liu Shu they called the Three Lords—lords, meaning the men an age holds up as its exemplars;

sentences.zh: 李膺、荀翌、杜宻、王暢、劉祐、魏朗、趙典、朱㝢為八俊，俊者，言人之英也；

translations.literal: Li Ying, Xun Yi, Du Mi, Wang Chang, Liu You, Wei Lang, Zhao Dian, and Zhu Yu were the Eight Talents—'talent' meaning the finest of men;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying, Xun Yi, Du Mi, Wang Chang, Liu You, Wei Lang, Zhao Dian, and Zhu Yu were the Eight Talents—talents, meaning the finest men of their generation;

sentences.zh: 郭泰、范滂、尹勳、巴肅及南陽宗慈、陳留夏馥、汝南蔡衍、泰山羊陟為八顧，顧者，言能以德行引人者也；

translations.literal: Guo Tai, Fan Pang, Yin Xun, Ba Su, and Zong Ci of Nanyang, Xia Fu of Chenliu, Cai Yan of Runan, and Yang Zhi of Taishan were the Eight Guardians—'guardian' meaning those who can lead others by virtue and conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai, Fan Pang, Yin Xun, Ba Su, Zong Ci of Nanyang, Xia Fu of Chenliu, Cai Yan of Runan, and Yang Zhi of Taishan were called the Eight Guardians—guardians, men who drew others toward them through virtue and character;

sentences.zh: 張儉、翟超、岑晊、苑康及山陽劉表、汝南陳翔、魯國孔昱、山陽檀敷為八及，及者，言其能導人追宗者也；

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, Zhai Chao, Cen Zhi, Yuan Kang, Liu Biao of Shanyang, Chen Xiang of Runan, Kong Yu of Luguo, and Tan Fu of Shanyang were the Eight Peers—'peer' meaning those who can guide men to follow worthy models;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, Zhai Chao, Cen Zhi, Yuan Kang, Liu Biao of Shanyang, Chen Xiang of Runan, Kong Yu of Lu, and Tan Fu of Shanyang were the Eight Peers—peers, men who led others to emulate the worthy;

sentences.zh: 度尚及東平張邈、王孝、東郡劉儒、泰山胡母班、陳留秦周、魯國蕃向、東萊王章為八廚，廚者，言能以財救人者也。

translations.literal: Du Shang, Zhang Miao of Dongping, Wang Xiao, Liu Ru of Dongjun, Humu Ban of Taishan, Qin Zhou of Chenliu, Fan Xiang of Luguo, and Wang Zhang of Donglai were the Eight Granaries—'granary' meaning those who can save people with their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shang, Zhang Miao of Dongping, Wang Xiao, Liu Ru of Dong Commandery, Humu Ban of Taishan, Qin Zhou of Chenliu, Fan Xiang of Lu, and Wang Zhang of Donglai were the Eight Granaries—granaries, men who rescued others with their wealth.

sentences.zh: 及陳、竇用事，復舉拔膺等；

translations.literal: When Chen and Dou held power, they again promoted and raised up Ying and the others;
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan and Dou Wu came to power, they once again advanced Li Ying and his fellows;

sentences.zh: 陳、竇誅，膺等復廢。

translations.literal: When Chen and Dou were executed, Ying and the others were again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan and Dou Wu were killed, Li Ying and the others were stripped of office once more.

sentences.zh: 宦官疾惡膺等，每下詔書，輒申黨人之禁。

translations.literal: The eunuchs hated and detested Ying and the others; every time an edict was issued, they would again declare the prohibition against the partisans.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs loathed Li Ying and his circle, and in every edict they issued they renewed the ban on partisan association.

sentences.zh: 侯覽怨張儉尤甚，覽鄉人朱並素佞邪，為儉所棄，承覽意指，上書告儉與同鄉二十四人別相署號，共為部黨，圖危社稷，而儉為之魁。

translations.literal: Hou Lan hated Zhang Jian most deeply. Lan's fellow townsmen Zhu Bing had long been fawning and depraved; rejected by Jian, he took Lan's intent and submitted a memorial accusing Jian and twenty-four fellow townsmen of separately adopting titles, forming together a partisan faction, plotting to endanger the realm—and Jian was its leader.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan harbored a special hatred for Zhang Jian. Zhu Bing, a fellow townsman of Lan's, was by nature sycophantic and corrupt and had been spurned by Jian. Reading Lan's mind, he memorialized the throne that Jian and twenty-four men of their district had taken up separate titles and formed a partisan clique bent on subverting the state—with Jian as their ringleader.

sentences.zh: 詔刊章捕儉等。

translations.literal: An edict was issued publishing the list and arresting Jian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out, names published, commanding the arrest of Zhang Jian and his associates.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，大長秋曹節因此諷有司奏「諸鉤黨者故司空虞放及李膺、杜宻、朱㝢、荀翌、翟超、劉儒、范滂等，請下州郡考治。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Grand Director of Palace Affairs Cao Jie thereupon prompted the responsible officials to memorialize: "All those implicated in the partisan association—the former Minister of Works Yu Fang, Li Ying, Du Mi, Zhu Yu, Xun Yi, Zhai Chao, Liu Ru, Fan Pang, and others—should be sent down to the provinces and commanderies for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Cao Jie, Grand Director of the Palace Household, maneuvered the relevant offices into memorializing: "All those ensnared in the partisan inquiry—the former Minister of Works Yu Fang, Li Ying, Du Mi, Zhu Yu, Xun Yi, Zhai Chao, Liu Ru, Fan Pang, and others—should be handed over to the provinces and commanderies for trial and punishment."

sentences.zh: 」是時上年十四，問節等曰：「何以為鉤黨？

translations.literal: " At that time the Emperor was fourteen years old. He asked Jie and the others, "What does it mean to be implicated in a partisan association?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was then fourteen. He asked Cao Jie and the others, "What does it mean to be caught up in a partisan inquiry?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「鉤黨者，即黨人也。

translations.literal: " They answered, "Those implicated in a partisan association are simply partisans.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "To be implicated in a partisan association is to be a partisan.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「黨人何用為惡而欲誅之邪？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "What evil have the partisans done that you wish to execute them?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "What crime have these partisans committed that they must be put to death?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「皆相舉群輩，欲為不軌。

translations.literal: " They answered, "They all promote one another in groups, intending to act against the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "They band together and promote one another, scheming treason.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「不軌欲如何？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "What treason do they intend?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "What treason do they intend?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「欲圖社稷。

translations.literal: " They answered, "They intend to plot against the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "They mean to overthrow the state.

sentences.zh: 」上乃可其奏。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 或謂李膺曰：「可去矣！

translations.literal: Someone said to Li Ying, "You can flee!
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Li Ying, "You should flee!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「事不辭難，罪不逃刑，臣之節也。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Not declining difficult tasks, not fleeing from punishment for crimes—these are a minister's obligations.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "To refuse no duty however hard, to accept punishment rather than evade it—that is a subject's honor.

sentences.zh: 吾年已六十，死生有命，去將安之！

translations.literal: I am already sixty years old; life and death are ordained by fate—if I flee, where shall I go!
translations.idiomatic: I am sixty years old. Life and death are Heaven's decree—where could I flee?

sentences.zh: 」乃詣詔獄，考死；

translations.literal: " He thereupon went to the imperial prison and died under torture;
translations.idiomatic: " He went straight to the imperial prison and died under interrogation;

sentences.zh: 門生故吏並被禁錮。

translations.literal: his students and former subordinates were all subjected to detention.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples and former retainers were all barred from office.

sentences.zh: 侍御史蜀郡景毅子顧為膺門徒，未有錄牒，不及於譴，毅慨然曰：「本謂膺賢，遣子師之，豈可以漏脫名籍，苟安而已！

translations.literal: Censor Jing Yi of Shu commandery had a son Gu who was Ying's disciple; having no recorded dossier, he was not reached by punishment. Yi said with indignation, "I originally considered Ying worthy and sent my son to study under him—how can I slip through the registers and seek safety for myself alone!
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jing Yi of Shu Commandery had sent his son Gu to study under Li Ying. Gu's name appeared on no register, so he escaped punishment. Yi declared in anger, "I believed Ying a worthy man and entrusted my son to him—shall I slip through the rolls and save myself alone?

sentences.zh: 」遂自表免歸。

translations.literal: " He thereupon submitted a memorial requesting his own dismissal and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized the throne for his own dismissal and went home.

sentences.zh: 汝南督郵吳導受詔捕范滂，至征羌，抱詔書閉傳捨，伏床而泣，一縣不知所為。

translations.literal: Runan Chief Clerk Wu Dao received the edict to arrest Fan Pang; upon reaching Zhengyang, he clutched the edict, shut himself in the relay station quarters, lay face down on the bed weeping—the whole district did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dao, chief clerk of Runan, was ordered to arrest Fan Pang. At Zhengyang he shut himself in the post station, clutching the edict, weeping face down on his bed while the whole county stood paralyzed.

sentences.zh: 滂聞之曰：「必為我也。

translations.literal: Pang, hearing of it, said, "It must be for me.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang heard of it he said, "This must be for my sake.

sentences.zh: 」即自詣獄。

translations.literal: " He immediately went of his own accord to prison.
translations.idiomatic: " He went straight to the jail.

sentences.zh: 縣令郭揖大驚，出，解印綬，引與俱亡，曰：「天下大矣，子何為在此！

translations.literal: Magistrate Guo Yi was greatly alarmed; he came out, removed his seal and cord, and wanted to flee together with him, saying, "The world is vast—why must you remain here!
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Guo Yi was stunned. He came out, removed his seal of office, and tried to flee with Pang, crying, "The world is wide—why must you stay here!

sentences.zh: 」滂曰：「滂死則禍塞，何敢以罪累君。

translations.literal: " Pang said, "If Pang dies, the disaster will be sealed—how dare I let my crime implicate you.
translations.idiomatic: " Pang said, "My death will stop the calamity here. How could I let my guilt fall upon you?

sentences.zh: 又令老母流離乎！

translations.literal: And would that not also make my old mother wander in exile!
translations.idiomatic: And would that not also force my aged mother into exile?

sentences.zh: 」其母就與之訣，滂白母曰：「仲博孝敬，足以供養。

translations.literal: " His mother came to bid him farewell. Pang told his mother, "Zhongbo is filial and respectful—he can provide for you sufficiently.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother came to take her leave. Pang said to her, "Zhongbo is filial and dutiful—he can provide for you.

sentences.zh: 滂從龍舒君歸黃泉，存亡各得其所。

translations.literal: Pang follows Lord Longshu to the Yellow Springs; in life and in death each will have his place.
translations.idiomatic: I follow my father, Lord Longshu, to the Yellow Springs—in life and death we each have our place.

sentences.zh: 惟大人割不可忍之恩，勿增感戚！

translations.literal: Only let the Lady sever ties that cannot be endured and add no further grief!
translations.idiomatic: Only grant me this: set aside love that cannot be borne and add no grief to what cannot be changed!

sentences.zh: 」仲博者，滂弟也。

translations.literal: " Zhongbo was Pang's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongbo was Pang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 龍舒君者，滂父龍舒侯相顯也。

translations.literal: Lord Longshu was Pang's father Xian, Chancellor to the Marquis of Longshu.
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Longshu" was Pang's father Xian, who had served as Chancellor to the Marquis of Longshu.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「汝今得與李、杜齊名，死亦何恨！

translations.literal: The mother said, "Today you win fame equal to Li and Du—what regret can death hold!
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "You will share fame with Li and Du—what room is left for regret in death!

sentences.zh: 既有令名，復求壽考，可兼得乎！

translations.literal: Having already won a fine name, yet also seeking long life—can both be had together!
translations.idiomatic: You seek a noble name and a long life together—can any man have both?

sentences.zh: 」滂跪受教，再拜而辭。

translations.literal: " Pang knelt to receive her instruction, bowed twice, and took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: " Pang knelt to receive her words, bowed twice, and departed.

sentences.zh: 顧其子曰：「吾欲使汝為惡，惡不可為；

translations.literal: Turning to her son she said, "I wanted you to do evil—but evil cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: She turned to her son and said, "I might have wished you to do evil, but evil cannot be done;

sentences.zh: 使汝為善，則我不為惡。

translations.literal: if I wished you to do good, then I could not do evil.
translations.idiomatic: if I wished you to do good, I could not choose evil for myself.

sentences.zh: 」行路聞之，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: " Those who heard it on the road all wept.
translations.idiomatic: " Passersby who overheard wept without exception.

sentences.zh: 凡黨人死者百餘人，妻子皆徙邊，天下豪桀及儒學有行義者，宦官一切指為黨人；

translations.literal: In all, more than a hundred partisans died; their wives and children were all exiled to the frontier. Throughout the realm, bold spirits and Confucian scholars of upright conduct—the eunuchs indiscriminately denounced them all as partisans;
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred partisans died; their wives and children were banished to the frontier. Bold men and upright scholars everywhere—the eunuchs denounced them all as partisans;

sentences.zh: 有怨隙者，因相陷害，睚眥之忿，濫入黨中。

translations.literal: those with old grievances took the occasion to destroy one another; resentments over the smallest slights were recklessly swept into the partisan lists.
translations.idiomatic: Men with old grudges turned on one another; the slightest feud landed men on the partisan rolls.

sentences.zh: 州郡承旨，或有未嘗交關，亦離禍毒，其死、徙、廢、禁者又六七百人。

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies carried out the edicts; some who had never had contact with the accused also suffered calamity. Those who died, were exiled, dismissed, or detained numbered six or seven hundred more.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces obeyed. Some who had never even met the accused were swept up in the ruin. Death, exile, dismissal, and detention claimed six or seven hundred more.

sentences.zh: 郭泰聞黨人已死，私為之慟曰：「《詩》云：『人之云亡，邦國殄瘁。

translations.literal: Guo Tai, hearing the partisans were dead, mourned them in private, saying, "The Book of Songs says: 'When good men perish, the state and realm waste away.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Tai learned the partisans were dead, he grieved privately, quoting the Book of Songs: "When good men perish, the realm withers.

sentences.zh: 』漢室滅矣，但未知『瞻烏爰止，於誰之屋』耳！

translations.literal: ' The House of Han is extinguished—but who can yet say 'The crow gazes and alights—at whose house?'!
translations.idiomatic: "The Han dynasty is finished. Only one question remains: 'The crow looks and settles—on whose roof?'"

sentences.zh: 」泰雖好臧否人倫，而不為危言核論，故能處濁世而怨禍不及焉。

translations.literal: " Though Tai liked to appraise the moral worth of men, he never spoke dangerous or incisive judgments; therefore he could dwell in a corrupt age without resentment or calamity reaching him.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Tai appraised men's character but never spoke recklessly or with dangerous severity, and so weathered a corrupt age unscathed.

sentences.zh: 張儉亡命困迫，望門投止，莫不重其名行，破家相容。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, fleeing for his life in desperate straits, knocked at every door seeking refuge; none failed to honor his fame and conduct, ruining their own households to shelter him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian fled for his life, knocking at every door. All honored his repute and risked ruin to shelter him.

sentences.zh: 後流轉東萊，止李篤家。

translations.literal: Later he wandered to Donglai and lodged at Li Du's home.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually made his way to Donglai and took refuge with Li Du.

sentences.zh: 外黃令毛欽操兵到門，篤引欽就席曰：「張儉負罪亡命，篤豈得藏之！

translations.literal: The magistrate of Waihuang, Mao Qin, came to the door with armed men. Du led Qin to a seat and said, "Zhang Jian bears guilt and flees for his life—how could Du conceal him!
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qin, magistrate of Waihuang, arrived at the door with soldiers. Du sat him down and said, "Zhang Jian is a fugitive with a price on his head—how could I hide him!

sentences.zh: 若審在此，此人名士，明廷寧宜執之乎！

translations.literal: If he is indeed here—this man is a renowned scholar—would Your Honor truly think it right to arrest him!
translations.idiomatic: If he is truly here, consider: he is a man of fame and principle. Would Your Honor truly arrest him?

sentences.zh: 」欽因起撫篤曰：「蘧伯玉恥獨為君子，足下如何專取仁義！

translations.literal: " Qin thereupon rose and patted Du, saying, "Qu Boyu would be ashamed to be the only gentleman—how can you monopolize all the righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: " Qin rose and clasped Du's hand. "Qu Boyu was ashamed to be the only gentleman—why should you keep all the honor for yourself!

sentences.zh: 」篤曰：「今欲分之，明廷載半去矣。

translations.literal: " Du said, "If you wish to share now, Your Honor carries half away already.
translations.idiomatic: " Du said, "Share him with me now and you take half the credit.

sentences.zh: 」欽歎息而去。

translations.literal: " Qin sighed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Qin sighed and left.

sentences.zh: 篤導儉經北海戲子然家，遂入漁陽出塞。

translations.literal: Du guided Jian through Beihai to Xi Ziran's home, then into Yuyang and out beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du guided Zhang Jian via Beihai and Xi Ziran's home, then through Yuyang and across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其所經歷，伏重誅者以十數，連引收考者布遍天下，宗親並皆殄滅，郡縣為之殘破。

translations.literal: Where he passed, those executed on his account numbered more than ten; those chained and interrogated through connection with him spread throughout the realm; kin were all extinguished; commanderies and districts were left in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he had stayed, more than ten hosts were executed. Investigations swept the empire; whole clans were destroyed; counties and commanderies lay in wreckage.

sentences.zh: 儉與魯國孔褒有舊，亡抵褒，不遇，褒弟融，年十六，匿之。

translations.literal: Jian had old ties with Kong Bao of Lu; fleeing, he came to Bao's home but did not find him. Bao's younger brother Rong, sixteen years old, hid him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian was old friends with Kong Bao of Lu. He fled to Bao's house but missed him; Bao's sixteen-year-old brother Rong hid him instead.

sentences.zh: 後事洩，儉得亡走，國相收褒、融送獄，未知所坐。

translations.literal: Later the matter leaked out; Jian managed to flee. The kingdom Chancellor arrested Bao and Rong and sent them to prison, not knowing whom to charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter came out, Jian escaped. The kingdom Chancellor arrested Bao and Rong; none could say which should bear guilt.

sentences.zh: 融曰：「保納捨藏者，融也，當坐。

translations.literal: Rong said, "The one who sheltered and concealed him is Rong—I should bear the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "I sheltered him—I alone am guilty.

sentences.zh: 」褒曰：「彼來求我，非弟之過。

translations.literal: " Bao said, "He came to seek me—it is not my younger brother's fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao said, "He came for me—not my brother's fault.

sentences.zh: 」吏問其母，母曰：「家事任長，妾當其辜。

translations.literal: " The officers questioned their mother. The mother said, "Household affairs rest with the eldest son—this concubine-wife should bear the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " The officers questioned their mother. She said, "The elder son runs the household—the guilt is mine.

sentences.zh: 」一門爭死，郡縣疑不能決，乃上讞之，詔書竟坐褒。

translations.literal: " The whole household contended to die; the commandery and district, unable to decide, submitted the case upward; the edict ultimately held Bao responsible.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole family vied to die for the others. The local authorities could not decide and referred the case upward; in the end Kong Bao was condemned.

sentences.zh: 及黨禁解，儉乃還鄉里，後為衛尉，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: When the partisan prohibition was lifted, Jian returned to his home village. Later he served as Minister of the Guards and died at eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the partisan ban was lifted, Zhang Jian returned home. He later served as Minister of the Guards and died at eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 夏馥聞張儉亡命，歎曰：「孽自己作，空污良善，一人逃死，禍及萬家，何以生為！

translations.literal: Xia Fu, hearing Zhang Jian had fled for his life, sighed, "The calamity was of my own making; I have vainly stained the good and innocent—one man flees death and calamity reaches ten thousand households. What point is there in living!
translations.idiomatic: Xia Fu, hearing of Zhang Jian's flight, sighed, "I brought this ruin on myself and have only stained the innocent. One man runs and ten thousand households suffer. Why go on living?

sentences.zh: 」乃自翦鬚變形，入林慮山中，隱姓名，為冶家傭，親突煙炭，形貌毀瘁，積二三年，人無知者。

translations.literal: " He cut off his beard and altered his appearance, entered Mount Linlu, hid his name, and hired himself out to a metalworker's household, personally tending the bellows and coal; his appearance wasted and ruined. After two or three years, no one knew him.
translations.idiomatic: " He cut his beard, altered his features, and withdrew to Mount Linlu under a false name, hiring himself to a smith and tending the forge until his body was broken. For two or three years no one recognized him.

sentences.zh: 馥弟靜載縑帛追求餉之，馥不受曰：「弟奈何載禍相餉乎！

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Jing loaded silk and cloth and sought him out to supply him. Fu refused, saying, "Younger brother, how can you carry calamity to me as provisions!
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jing found him with silks and goods. Fu refused them: "Brother, would you bring catastrophe to me as a gift?

sentences.zh: 」黨禁未解而卒。

translations.literal: " Before the partisan prohibition was lifted, he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died before the partisan ban was lifted.

sentences.zh: 初，中常侍張讓父死，歸葬穎川，雖一郡畢至，而名士無往者，讓甚恥之，陳寔獨弔焉。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Regular Attendant Zhang Rang's father died and was returned to Yingchuan for burial, though the whole commandery assembled, not one renowned scholar went; Rang was deeply shamed. Chen Shi alone made mourning calls.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Zhang Rang's father died and was buried in Yingchuan, the whole commandery turned out—but no man of reputation attended, to Rang's shame. Chen Shi alone paid his respects.

sentences.zh: 及誅黨人，讓以寔故，多所全宥。

translations.literal: When the partisans were condemned to death, Rang on Shi's account spared many.
translations.idiomatic: When the partisans were marked for death, Zhang Rang spared many for Chen Shi's sake.

sentences.zh: 南陽何顒，素與陳蕃、李膺善，亦被收捕，乃變名姓匿汝南間，與袁紹為奔走之交，常私入雒陽，從紹計議，為諸名士罹黨事者求救援，設權計，使得逃隱，所全免甚眾。

translations.literal: He Yong of Nanyang had long been on good terms with Chen Fan and Li Ying and was also sought for arrest; he changed his name and hid in the region of Runan, becoming Yuan Shao's close companion in urgent affairs. He often entered Luoyang in secret, consulted with Shao, and sought rescue for renowned scholars caught in the partisan affair, devising stratagems so they could escape and hide—the number he preserved was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He Yong of Nanyang, a friend of Chen Fan and Li Ying, was also hunted. He changed his name and hid in Runan, where he became Yuan Shao's closest ally. He slipped into Luoyang in secret, plotted with Shao, and engineered escapes for scholars caught in the purge—saving a great many.

sentences.zh: 初，太尉袁湯三子，成、逢、隗。

translations.literal: Initially, Grand Marshal Yuan Tang had three sons: Cheng, Sui, and Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yuan Tang had three sons: Cheng, Sui, and Kui.

sentences.zh: 成生紹，逢生術。

translations.literal: Cheng fathered Shao; Sui fathered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was the father of Yuan Shao; Sui was the father of Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 逢、隗皆有名稱，少歷顯官。

translations.literal: Sui and Kui both had famous reputations and in youth held eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Kui were both well known and had held high office early in life.

sentences.zh: 時中常侍袁赦以逢、隗宰相家，與之同姓，推崇以為外援，故袁氏貴寵於世，富奢甚，不與它公族同。

translations.literal: At the time the Regular Attendant Yuan She, seeing that Sui and Kui came from a prime-ministerial house and shared the same surname, upheld them as his external support; therefore the Yuan clan was honored and favored in the world, extravagantly wealthy, not the same as other noble clans.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yuan She, sharing the clan name, championed Sui and Kui as family allies of a great ministerial house. The Yuans flourished—wealthy beyond other noble lines.

sentences.zh: 紹壯健有威容，愛士養名，賓客輻湊歸之，輜軿、柴轂，填接街陌。

translations.literal: Shao was strong and robust with a commanding presence; he cherished scholars and cultivated reputation; guests gathered and flocked to him—covered carriages and plain carts filled and packed the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao was imposing in bearing, cultivated scholars and reputation, and drew crowds of retainers—carriages choked the streets around his gates.

sentences.zh: 術亦以俠氣聞。

translations.literal: Shu was also known for chivalrous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was known for his swashbuckling spirit.

sentences.zh: 逢從兄子閎，少有操行，以耕學為業，逢、隗數饋之，無所受。

translations.literal: Sui's paternal first cousin's son Hong, from youth possessed conduct and integrity, made farming and study his occupation; Sui and Kui repeatedly sent him gifts—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, a cousin's son in Sui's branch, lived by farming and study from youth. Sui and Kui sent him gifts repeatedly; he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 閎見時方險亂，而家門富盛，常對兄弟歎曰：「吾先公福祚，後世不能以德守之，而競為驕奢，與亂世爭權，此即晉之三郤矣。

translations.literal: Hong, seeing the times were dangerously turbulent while his household was rich and flourishing, often sighed to his brothers, "Our forefather's blessings—later generations cannot guard them with virtue but instead compete in arrogance and extravagance, vying for power in chaotic times. This is precisely the Three Xi family of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hong watched troubled times and a rich household and often warned his brothers: "Our ancestor's blessings—yet our kin guard them with pride, not virtue, grasping for power in chaos. This is the Three Xi of Jin all over again.

sentences.zh: 」及黨事起，閎欲投跡深林，以母老，不宜遠遁，乃築土室四周於庭，不為戶，自牖納飲食。

translations.literal: " When the partisan affair arose, Hong wished to withdraw to deep forests, but because his mother was old it was not fitting to flee far; he therefore built an earthen chamber on all four sides of the courtyard, making no door, receiving food and drink through the window.
translations.idiomatic: " When the purge began, Hong wished to vanish into the wilds, but his mother was aged, so instead he built an earthen cell in the courtyard with no door, taking food through the window.

sentences.zh: 母思閎時，往就視，母去，便自掩閉，兄弟妻子莫得見也。

translations.literal: When his mother missed Hong she would go to look at him; when she left, he would shut himself in again; brothers, wife, and children could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother missed him she would visit at the window; when she left he sealed himself in again. Not even wife or brothers could see him.

sentences.zh: 潛身十八年，卒於土室。

translations.literal: He concealed himself eighteen years and died in the earthen chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He lived hidden eighteen years and died in his earthen cell.

sentences.zh: 初，范滂等非訐朝政，自公卿以下皆折節下之，太學生爭慕其風，以為文學將興，處士復用。

translations.literal: Initially, Fan Pang and the others did not denounce court politics, yet from the Three Dukes downward all lowered themselves in deference; Imperial University students competed to emulate their style, thinking that literature would flourish and recluses would be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Pang and his circle did not openly attack the court, yet from the highest ministers down all deferred to them. University students emulated them, believing learning would flourish and worthy recluses would serve again.

sentences.zh: 申屠蟠獨歎曰：「昔戰國之世，處士橫議，列國之王至為擁彗先驅，卒有坑儒燒書之禍，今之謂矣。

translations.literal: Shen Tu Pan alone sighed, "In the Warring States age, recluses spoke freely across the land; kings of the various states even held brooms and went before them as guides—yet in the end came the calamity of burying scholars and burning books. The same will be said of today.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tu Pan alone warned: "In the Warring States, freelance scholars held forth and kings swept paths before them—and it ended in buried scholars and burnt books. The same is coming now.

sentences.zh: 」乃絕跡於梁、碭之間，因樹為屋，自同傭人。

translations.literal: " He thereupon vanished between Liang and Dang, making a dwelling from trees, counting himself the same as a hired laborer.
translations.idiomatic: " He vanished into the wilds between Liang and Dang, built a hut from branches, and lived like a hired hand.

sentences.zh: 居二年，滂等果罹黨錮之鍋，唯蟠超然免於評論。

translations.literal: After two years, Pang and the others indeed suffered the calamity of the partisan prohibition; only Pan, detached and aloof, escaped being judged and criticized.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Fan Pang and the rest were indeed caught in the calamity of the partisan proscription—only Pan, keeping his distance, escaped the reckoning.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：天下有道，君子揚於王庭，以正小人之罪，而莫敢不服；

translations.literal: Minister Guang said: When the realm has the Way, the gentleman holds forth in the royal court to correct the crimes of petty men, and none dares fail to submit;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: When the realm is governed by the Way, gentlemen speak openly at court to judge petty men's crimes, and no one dares rebel;

sentences.zh: 天下無道，君子囊括不言，以避小人之禍，而猶或不免。

translations.literal: when the realm lacks the Way, the gentleman wraps himself in silence to avoid the calamity of petty men—and still may not escape.
translations.idiomatic: when the realm has lost the Way, gentlemen hold their tongues to avoid petty men's vengeance—and still may not escape.

sentences.zh: 黨人生昏亂之世，不在其位，四海橫流，而欲以口舌救之，臧否人物，激濁揚清，撩虺蛇之頭，踐虎狼之屬，以至身被淫刑，禍及朋友，士類殲滅而國隨以亡，不亦悲乎！

translations.literal: The partisans were born into an age of confusion and disorder, not in their proper posts; the four seas flowed askew—yet they wished to save it with words alone, praising and blaming men, stirring the clear and agitating the muddy, rousing the head of vipers and serpents, treading on the kindred of tigers and wolves—until their bodies received cruel punishment, calamity reached their friends, the scholar class was extinguished and the state followed into ruin—is this not tragic!
translations.idiomatic: The partisans lived in a fallen age, out of office, with chaos everywhere—yet they hoped to save the realm with words alone, praising and condemning, stirring up what was filthy and what was pure, rousing vipers and treading on tigers. They earned torture, destroyed their friends, wiped out the scholar class, and the state followed into ruin. What tragedy!

sentences.zh: 夫唯郭泰既明且哲，以保其身，申屠蟠見幾而作，不俟終日，卓乎其不可及已！

translations.literal: Only Guo Tai, both discerning and wise, preserved his person; Shen Tu Pan, seeing the signs and acting, did not wait even a full day—how surpassing, beyond reach!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai alone was wise enough to preserve himself; Shen Tu Pan saw the turning point and acted without delay—how far beyond the rest!

sentences.zh: 庚子晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of geng-zi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the geng-zi cycle the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，太尉劉寵免；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Grand Marshal Liu Chong was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Grand Marshal Liu Chong was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 太僕扶溝郭禧為太尉。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Transport Guo Xi of Fugou was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xi of Fugou, Director of the Imperial Transport, was appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇并州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 長樂太僕曹節病困，詔拜車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Changletai Cao Jie, gravely ill, was by edict appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie, Chancellor of Changletai, lay gravely ill and was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry by edict.

sentences.zh: 有頃，疾瘳，上印綬，復為中常侍，位特進，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: Before long his illness recovered; he returned the seal and cord and again became Regular Attendant, with position of Special Advance and salary of middle two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon recovered, returned the seal, and resumed his post as Regular Attendant with the rank of Special Advance and salary of middle two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 高句驪王伯固寇遼東，玄菟太守耿臨討降之。

translations.literal: The king of Goguryeo, Bogu, raided Liaodong; Grand Administrator of Xuantu Geng Lin attacked and received his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu, king of Goguryeo, raided Liaodong. Geng Lin, Grand Administrator of Xuantu, attacked and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，丙寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on the last day of bing-yin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, on the last day of bing-yin, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 征段熲還京師，拜侍中。

translations.literal: Duan Jiong was recalled from campaign to the capital and appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong was recalled to the capital and appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 熲在邊十餘年，未嘗一日蓐寢，與將士同甘苦，故皆樂為死戰，所向有功。

translations.literal: Jiong was on the frontier more than ten years, never once sleeping on a mat, sharing hardship and comfort with officers and soldiers; therefore all gladly fought to the death for him, and wherever he went there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong spent more than ten years on the frontier, never once sleeping in comfort, sharing every hardship with his men. They fought willingly to the death for him, and his campaigns never failed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，太尉郭禧罷；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Grand Marshal Guo Xi was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Grand Marshal Guo Xi was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以太中大夫聞人襲為太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Wenren Xi was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Wenren Xi was appointed Grand Marshal in his place.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，司空劉囂罷；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Liu Xiao was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Liu Xiao was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 八月，以大鴻臚梁國橋玄為司空。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qiao Xuan of Liang State, Grand Herald, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Qiao Xuan of Liang State, Grand Herald, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 九月，執金吾董寵坐矯永樂太后屬請，下獄死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Dong Chong, Commandant of the Capital Guard, was convicted for forging petitions in Empress Dowager Yongle's name, was thrown into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Dong Chong, Commandant of the Capital Guard, was found guilty of using forged petitions in Empress Dowager Yongle's name, was imprisoned, and died there.

sentences.zh: 冬，鬱林太守谷永以恩信招降烏滸人十餘萬，皆內屬，受冠帶，開置七縣。

translations.literal: In winter, Gu Yong, Grand Administrator of Yulin, by kindness and good faith summoned and reduced more than a hundred thousand Wuhu people; all submitted to inner allegiance, received caps and sashes, and seven counties were newly established.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Gu Yong, Grand Administrator of Yulin, won over more than a hundred thousand Wuhu people through kindness and trust; they all submitted to Han rule, received official caps and sashes, and seven new counties were established.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史扶風孟佗遣從事任涉將敦煌兵五百人，與戊己司馬曹寬、西域長史張宴將焉耆、龜茲、車師前、後部，合三萬餘人討疏，攻楨中城，四十餘日不能下，引去。

translations.literal: Meng Tuo of Fufeng, Inspector of Liang Province, sent his aide Ren She leading five hundred Dunhuang troops, together with Cao Kuan, Wuji Commandant, and Zhang Yan, Chief Clerk of the Western Regions, leading the Qiuci, Kucha, and Front and Rear Divisions of the Cheshi—more than thirty thousand men in all—to punish Shule, attacked Zhongzhong city, and after more than forty days could not take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tuo of Fufeng, Inspector of Liang Province, dispatched his aide Ren She with five hundred Dunhuang troops, and together with Wuji Commandant Cao Kuan and Chief Clerk of the Western Regions Zhang Yan, who led forces from Qiuci, Kucha, and the Front and Rear Divisions of the Cheshi, more than thirty thousand men in all, marched against Shule and besieged Zhongzhong city. After more than forty days they failed to capture it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後疏勒王連相殺害，朝廷亦不能復治。

translations.literal: After this the kings of Shule murdered one another in succession, and the court also could not restore governance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the kings of Shule slew one another in turn, and the court could no longer restore order there.

sentences.zh: 初，中常侍張讓有監奴，典任家事，威形喧赫。

translations.literal: Initially, the Regular Attendant Zhang Rang had a steward slave who managed household affairs; his prestige and bearing were clamorous and dazzling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Regular Attendant Zhang Rang kept a steward slave who ran his household affairs, and whose power and presence were loud and overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 孟佗資產饒贍，與奴朋結，傾竭饋問，無所遺愛。

translations.literal: Meng Tuo's assets were rich and ample; he formed a bond with the slave, exhausting all in gifts and inquiries, leaving no generosity withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tuo was wealthy and well supplied; he befriended the slave, lavished gifts upon him without stint, and withheld nothing.

sentences.zh: 奴咸德之，問其所欲。

translations.literal: The slave was all grateful to him and asked what he desired.
translations.idiomatic: The slave was deeply grateful and asked what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 佗曰：「吾望汝曹為我一拜耳！

translations.literal: Tuo said, "I only wish you all would bow once for me!
translations.idiomatic: Tuo said, "All I want is for you to bow to me once!

sentences.zh: 」時賓客求謁讓者，車常數百千兩，佗詣讓，後至，不得進，監奴乃率諸倉頭迎拜於路，遂共輿車入門，賓客咸驚，謂佗善於讓，皆爭以珍玩賂之。

translations.literal: " At the time guests seeking audience with Rang—carriages often numbered in the hundreds and thousands—Tuo went to Rang's, arriving late, and could not enter; the steward slave then led the various head stewards to bow in reception on the road, and together they carried the carriage through the gate; the guests were all astonished, thinking Tuo was skilled with Rang, and all competed to bribe him with precious curios.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time, visitors seeking an audience with Rang often lined the road with hundreds or thousands of carriages. When Tuo arrived late and could not get in, the steward slave led the head stewards out to bow to him in the street, and together they carried his carriage through the gate. The guests were astonished, assuming Tuo was on excellent terms with Rang, and all vied to ply him with precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 佗分以遺讓，讓大喜，由是以佗為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Tuo divided them and gave them to Rang; Rang was greatly pleased, and thereby made Tuo Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo shared the gifts with Rang, who was delighted and thereupon had him appointed Inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，帝加元服，赦天下，唯黨人不赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiazi day, the emperor assumed the capping ceremony, pardoned all under Heaven, and only the partisans were not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiazi day, the emperor came of age, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, but the partisans alone were excluded.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸卯，地震。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guimao day, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guimao day, the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of xinyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of xinyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太尉聞人襲免；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wenren Xi was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wenren Xi was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以太僕汝南李咸為太尉。

translations.literal: Li Xian of Runan, Director of Imperial Transport, was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian of Runan, Director of the Imperial Transport, was appointed Grand Marshal in his place.

sentences.zh: 大疫。

translations.literal: A great epidemic.
translations.idiomatic: A great plague broke out.

sentences.zh: 司徒許訓免；

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Xu Xun was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Xu Xun was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以司空橋玄為司徒；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Qiao Xuan was made Minister over the Masses;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Qiao Xuan was appointed Minister over the Masses;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以太常南陽來艷為司空。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Lai Yan of Nanyang, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Lai Yan of Nanyang, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，司空來艷免。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Lai Yan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Lai Yan was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，立貴人宋氏為皇后，後，執金吾酆之女也。

translations.literal: On guichou day, Noble Lady Song was established as empress; the empress was the daughter of Feng, Commandant of the Capital Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day, Noble Lady Song was made empress; she was the daughter of Feng, Commandant of the Capital Guard.

sentences.zh: 司徒橋玄免；

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Qiao Xuan was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Qiao Xuan was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以太常南陽宗俱為司空，前司空許栩為司徒。

translations.literal: Zong Ju of Nanyang, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was made Minister of Works; former Minister of Works Xu Xu was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ju of Nanyang, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed Minister of Works, and former Minister of Works Xu Xu became Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 帝以竇太后有援立之功，

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered that Empress Dowager Dou had the merit of supporting his enthronement,
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor felt that Empress Dowager Dou had helped put him on the throne,

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊子朔，率群臣朝太后於南宮，親饋上壽。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of wuzi, he led the court officials to attend upon the empress dowager at the Southern Palace and personally served her the longevity toast.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of wuzi, he led the court to pay homage to the empress dowager at the Southern Palace and personally offered her the toast of long life.

sentences.zh: 黃門令董萌因此數為太后訴冤，帝深納之，供養資奉，有加於前。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng thereupon repeatedly pleaded the empress dowager's grievances for her; the emperor deeply accepted this, and her provisions and support were increased beyond what they had been before.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng repeatedly pressed the empress dowager's case before the emperor, who took it deeply to heart and increased her stipends and support beyond what she had received before.

sentences.zh: 曹節、王甫疾之，誣萌以謗訕永樂宮，下獄死。

translations.literal: Cao Jie and Wang Fu hated this, slandered Meng with maligning Yongle Palace, had him thrown into prison, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie and Wang Fu resented this, falsely accused Dong Meng of slandering Yongle Palace, had him imprisoned, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑寇并州。

translations.literal: The Xianbei raided Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei raided Bing Province.
